choices.text: Genetic testing for Y chromosome microdeletion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Intrauterine insemination with his ejaculated sperm

explanation.summary: Azoospermia is a critical semen analysis finding that warrants genetic testing for Y chromosome microdeletion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Azoospermia, the complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate, warrants genetic testing for Y chromosome microdeletion. The finding has already been confirmed on two analyses obtained at least one month apart, satisfying the recommendation for repeat testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two analyses at least one month apart already confirm the finding; further repetition delays the indicated genetic workup.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Exogenous testosterone is listed among medication exposures sought in the male infertility history as a contributor, not a treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cystic fibrosis testing is prompted by absence of the vas deferens on examination, which this patient does not have.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IUI places washed, concentrated sperm in the uterus and cannot work when the ejaculate contains no sperm.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with anovulatory infertility is prescribed letrozole. Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which this medication promotes ovulation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acts as a direct FSH analog on developing ovarian follicles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antagonizes estrogen receptors in both the hypothalamus and the pituitary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blocks progesterone receptors within the secretory endometrium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enhances estrogen negative feedback on the anterior pituitary

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibits aromatase, decreasing estrogen synthesis and negative feedback

explanation.summary: Letrozole is an aromatase inhibitor that lowers estrogen synthesis, releasing the hypothalamic-pituitary axis from negative feedback and increasing FSH.
explanation.whyCorrect: Letrozole decreases estrogen synthesis by inhibiting the aromatase-mediated conversion of androgens to estrogens. The reduced estrogenic negative feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary axis increases FSH release, promoting follicular development and ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Letrozole raises endogenous FSH secretion indirectly; it is not a gonadotropin analog acting on follicles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Estrogen receptor antagonism at the hypothalamus and pituitary is the mechanism of clomiphene, a selective estrogen receptor modulator.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Letrozole acts on aromatase in the estrogen synthesis pathway, not on progesterone receptors in the endometrium.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Letrozole reduces, rather than enhances, estrogen negative feedback; enhancing feedback would suppress FSH and ovulation.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman and her partner have unexplained infertility after a complete evaluation of both partners. They elect to proceed with intrauterine insemination. To improve pregnancy rates in this situation, IUI should be performed in combination with which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A course of empiric antibiotics

choices.label: B
choices.text: Insemination with unwashed fresh semen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ovulation stimulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Strict bed rest after each insemination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transfer of a cultured embryo

explanation.summary: For unexplained infertility, IUI should be combined with ovulation stimulation because IUI alone does not increase pregnancy rates in this population.
explanation.whyCorrect: IUI involves placing washed, concentrated sperm directly into the uterus around the time of ovulation, with per-cycle pregnancy rates of roughly 10-15%. In unexplained infertility, it should be administered together with ovulation stimulation, since IUI alone does not raise pregnancy rates in this group.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Antibiotics are not a component of the IUI protocol described and do not address the reason IUI alone underperforms here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IUI specifically uses washed, concentrated sperm; unwashed semen is not part of the procedure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bed rest is not part of the described technique and does not substitute for ovulation stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Embryo culture and transfer belong to in vitro fertilization, a different treatment from IUI.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman comes to the office because she has not conceived after 14 months of regular, unprotected intercourse with her husband. Three years ago she had an uncomplicated vaginal delivery of a healthy infant. Her menstrual cycles occur regularly every 28 days. Which of the following best describes this couple's situation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anovulatory infertility

choices.label: B
choices.text: Normal fertility not yet meeting criteria for evaluation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Primary infertility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Secondary infertility

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unexplained infertility

explanation.summary: Secondary infertility is the inability to achieve pregnancy after a previous pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Infertility is the inability to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of regular, unprotected intercourse, and this couple has passed that threshold. Because she previously achieved a pregnancy, her condition is classified as secondary infertility rather than primary infertility.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Her regular monthly cycles argue against ovulatory dysfunction, and no evaluation has established a cause.
whyWrongByChoice.B: At 14 months of regular, unprotected intercourse she has exceeded the 12-month definition, so evaluation is warranted.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Primary infertility refers to never having achieved a pregnancy; she has a prior delivery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Unexplained infertility can only be assigned after a complete evaluation of both partners fails to identify a cause; no workup has been done yet.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A physician counsels a couple beginning an infertility evaluation about the most common identifiable causes of infertility. Among female factors specifically, ovulatory disorders account for approximately what percentage of infertility diagnoses?

explanation.summary: Ovulatory disorders account for approximately 25% of infertility diagnoses among female factors.
explanation.whyCorrect: The three most common identifiable causes of infertility are ovulatory dysfunction, male factor, and tubal disease. Among female factors specifically, ovulatory disorders account for approximately 25% of infertility diagnoses, which is why the workup includes assessment for ovulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% substantially understates the contribution of ovulatory disorders to female-factor infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 15% is below the approximately 25% figure attributed to ovulatory disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Half of female-factor diagnoses overstates the share of ovulatory disorders; other causes such as tubal disease also contribute.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Three-quarters far exceeds the stated proportion; ovulatory dysfunction is common but not that dominant.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman comes to the clinic for a routine visit. She reports that she and her partner rely on withdrawal as their only method of pregnancy prevention and asks how likely the method is to fail. Which of the following failure rates per year is most accurate for this method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less than 1%

explanation.summary: Withdrawal is a Tier III method with an 18-28% failure rate per year.
explanation.whyCorrect: Withdrawal belongs to Tier III of contraceptive effectiveness, along with barrier methods and fertility-based methods, all of which carry an 18-28% failure rate per year. Counseling should weigh this efficacy against patient preferences and adherence.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A failure rate below 1% per year describes Tier I methods: LARCs and permanent sterilization.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 3-5% does not correspond to any of the effectiveness tiers described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 6-12% per year is the Tier II range, which covers combined hormonal contraceptives, progestin-only pills, and depot medroxyprogesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 40-50% overstates the failure rate; even the least effective tier is 18-28% per year.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman who does not want hormonal contraception elects to use a fertility awareness-based method with her partner. This approach prevents pregnancy primarily by which of the following mechanisms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocking sperm from entering the upper reproductive tract with a physical barrier

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inactivating sperm within the lower reproductive tract with spermicidal agents

choices.label: C
choices.text: Monitoring cyclic signs of ovulation to identify the days when conception is possible

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preventing implantation by continuously altering the endometrial lining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppressing ovulation through sustained hormonal negative feedback

explanation.summary: Fertility awareness-based methods work by monitoring fertility signs during the menstrual cycle to identify the fertile window.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fertility awareness-based methods involve monitoring fertility signs during the menstrual cycle to identify the fertile window so intercourse can be timed to avoid it. They are grouped with barrier methods and withdrawal in Tier III effectiveness (18-28% failure per year).

whyWrongByChoice.A: Physical blockade of sperm from the upper reproductive tract is the mechanism of barrier methods, not fertility awareness.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Spermicidal agents are part of barrier-method contraception, not fertility awareness.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fertility awareness methods do not modify the endometrium; they rely on timing intercourse around the fertile window.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ovulation suppression is a mechanism of hormonal contraception; fertility awareness methods do not alter the cycle.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A postpartum clinic is designing a counseling program to reduce interpregnancy intervals shorter than 6 months and views the effort as an opportunity to address health inequities. Which of the following groups is at highest risk for the shortest interpregnancy intervals?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Females in nonheterosexual partnerships seeking pregnancy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Females of higher socioeconomic status and greater income

choices.label: C
choices.text: Females of lower socioeconomic status and females of color

choices.label: D
choices.text: Females older than 35 years at the time of conception

choices.label: E
choices.text: Females with chronic medical conditions requiring therapy

explanation.summary: Females of lower socioeconomic status and females of color are at highest risk for the shortest interpregnancy intervals.
explanation.whyCorrect: Females of lower socioeconomic status and females of color are at higher risk for the shortest interpregnancy intervals, making interval counseling an opportunity to address health inequities. Counseling should use shared decision-making, recognizing that birth-spacing decisions are multifactorial and include age, fertility aspirations, and personal circumstances.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Nonheterosexual partnership is a criterion for earlier infertility evaluation, not a risk factor for short interpregnancy intervals.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Higher socioeconomic status is not identified as a risk factor for short interpregnancy intervals; the disparity runs in the opposite direction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Older age may factor into a patient's own spacing decisions, but age over 35 is not the group identified as highest risk for the shortest intervals.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chronic medical conditions are targets of preconception risk screening, not the population identified with the shortest intervals.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 23-year-old woman answers "no" when asked whether she would like to become pregnant in the next year and begins a contraceptive method of her choice. Which of the following best describes the recommended approach to pregnancy intention screening for this patient going forward?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Omit further screening while she is using contraception

choices.label: B
choices.text: Repeat screening a single time at her next annual examination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Repeat screening at encounters throughout her reproductive lifespan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat screening only if she requests preconception counseling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat screening only once she reaches 35 years of age

explanation.summary: Pregnancy intention screening should recur at patient encounters across the reproductive lifespan because health status and risk factors change over time.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pregnancy intention screening is a core component of primary preventive care that should occur at every encounter with reproductive-aged individuals and be repeated multiple times across the reproductive lifespan. Approximately 45-51% of pregnancies in the United States are unintended, and repeated screening creates recurring opportunities for education and optimization of reproductive outcomes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Contraceptive use does not end screening; intentions and risk factors change over time, which is why screening recurs.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A single repeat misses the recommendation for screening at multiple encounters across her reproductive years.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting for the patient to raise the topic defeats the purpose of routine screening at each encounter.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Screening applies to all individuals with reproductive potential throughout the lifespan, not only after a specific age.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman with a chronic medical condition comes to the office for preconception counseling. She takes a maintenance medication that is not ideal for use in pregnancy, but her specialist has determined that stopping it would be unsafe. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Advise that pregnancy is contraindicated while she requires the medication

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arrange a multidisciplinary discussion of risks, benefits, and risk reduction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Continue the medication and defer discussion until pregnancy is confirmed

choices.label: D
choices.text: Discontinue the medication once she begins trying to conceive

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replace the medication with an herbal supplement of similar effect

explanation.summary: When a medication that is not ideal for pregnancy cannot be stopped, a multidisciplinary approach should address risks, benefits, and risk reduction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Comprehensive medication review is an essential component of preconception care. Some medications are not ideal for pregnancy but cannot be stopped; in those situations a multidisciplinary approach is important to discuss risks, benefits, and risk reduction rather than unilateral discontinuation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The lecture's framework is risk discussion and reduction, not a blanket prohibition on pregnancy for patients on necessary medications.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Deferring the conversation until pregnancy is confirmed forfeits the preconception window in which risks can be weighed and reduced.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Her specialist has determined the medication cannot be safely stopped, so discontinuation at conception is not an option here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Supplements and herbal products themselves require review in preconception care; substituting one is not a described strategy.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A healthy 28-year-old woman and her 30-year-old husband request genetic screening at a preconception visit. Neither partner reports a family history of birth defects, genetic disorders, or mental disorders. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening approach?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decline testing because neither partner has a family history of genetic disease

choices.label: B
choices.text: Refer both partners to genetic counseling before offering any laboratory testing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Restrict testing to disorders already documented in either partner's family

choices.label: D
choices.text: Screen her for autosomal recessive traits, then screen him if she is a carrier

choices.label: E
choices.text: Screen him for autosomal recessive traits, then screen her if he is a carrier

explanation.summary: Preconception genetic screening typically screens the female for autosomal recessive traits first, then the male if she is a carrier.
explanation.whyCorrect: All patients seeking pregnancy should be counseled on and offered genetic testing. The typical approach is to screen the female for autosomal recessive traits and then screen the male partner if she is found to carry any trait.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Screening is offered to all patients seeking pregnancy, not just those with a positive family history.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Referral for genetic counseling is reasonable when a patient is a carrier or has a family history of a genetic condition; it is not a prerequisite for offering screening.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Family-history-directed testing supplements, rather than replaces, the routine offer of carrier screening to all patients seeking pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The described sequence starts with the female partner; the male is screened second, only if she is a carrier.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 29-year-old pregnant woman receives the inactivated influenza and Tdap vaccines during pregnancy. Which of the following best explains how this vaccination strategy protects her newborn against neonatal infection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fetal exposure to attenuated organisms contained in the vaccines

choices.label: B
choices.text: Passage of vaccine antigens across the placenta to immunize the fetus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Transfer of maternal lymphocytes into the fetal circulation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Transplacental transfer of maternal IgG antibodies

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transplacental transfer of maternal IgM antibodies

explanation.summary: Maternal vaccination protects the newborn through transplacental transfer of maternal IgG antibodies, providing passive immunity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Vaccination before or during pregnancy provides the newborn with passive immunity to neonatal infections through transplacental transfer of maternal IgG antibodies. Inactivated vaccines such as influenza and Tdap can be given safely during pregnancy specifically to maximize this passive antibody transfer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Influenza and Tdap given in pregnancy are inactivated vaccines; live attenuated vaccines are contraindicated during pregnancy precisely because of theoretical fetal infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The mechanism is transfer of maternal antibody, not direct fetal immunization by vaccine antigens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Passive neonatal protection from maternal vaccination is attributed to antibody transfer, not cellular transfer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The passive immunity described is mediated by maternal IgG, the antibody class transferred across the placenta.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman is found to be nonimmune to varicella at a preconception visit and receives the varicella vaccine the same day. According to the vaccine manufacturer's recommendation, she should wait how long after this vaccination before attempting to conceive?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2 weeks

choices.label: B
choices.text: 3 months

choices.label: C
choices.text: 6 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: 12 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: 28 days

explanation.summary: For varicella vaccination specifically, the manufacturer recommends waiting three months before pregnancy, longer than the general ACIP interval for live vaccines.
explanation.whyCorrect: ACIP recommends avoiding pregnancy for 28 days after each dose of a live vaccine because of potential fetal risk, but for varicella vaccination the manufacturer specifically recommends waiting three months. The question asks for the manufacturer's recommendation, making three months correct.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Two weeks is shorter than either the ACIP interval or the manufacturer's recommendation for varicella.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Six weeks does not match either the 28-day ACIP interval or the manufacturer's three-month recommendation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A full year of pregnancy avoidance is not recommended after any of the live vaccines discussed.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 28 days is the ACIP recommendation applied to live vaccines in general, not the varicella manufacturer's longer recommendation the question asks about.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman planning pregnancy asks whether her diet needs to change before she conceives. In addition to folic acid, adequate intake of which of the following nutrients is specifically emphasized in preconception nutritional counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Calcium and vitamin D

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iron and iodine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vitamin A and selenium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vitamin B12 and magnesium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin C and zinc

explanation.summary: Preconception nutritional optimization emphasizes adequate intake of folic acid, iron, and iodine.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nutritional optimization and supplementation are a critical component of preconception care, with adequate intake of essential nutrients — particularly folic acid, iron, and iodine — described as paramount. Balanced nutrition and regular physical activity for weight management are also emphasized to avoid complications of both underweight and overweight status.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Calcium and vitamin D are not the nutrients singled out alongside folic acid in preconception counseling.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vitamin A and selenium are not the emphasized pair; iron and iodine are.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Vitamin B12 and magnesium are not the nutrients highlighted with folic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vitamin C and zinc are not the emphasized preconception nutrients.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: During psychosocial screening at a preconception visit, a 27-year-old woman discloses ongoing intimate partner violence at home. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assess her immediate safety and connect her to community resources

choices.label: B
choices.text: Defer further discussion until she is actively trying to conceive

choices.label: C
choices.text: Provide written materials and revisit the topic at her next annual visit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure her that nothing she disclosed can be reported to anyone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recommend joint counseling sessions that include her partner

explanation.summary: When screening identifies ongoing abuse, the response is assessment of immediate safety, referral for further evaluation or intervention, and connection to community resources.
explanation.whyCorrect: When psychosocial screening identifies ongoing abuse or mental health concerns, assessment of immediate safety, referral for further evaluation or intervention, and connection to community resources should be provided. These psychosocial risks also affect the newborn's welfare and should be reassessed through pregnancy and postpartum planning.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ongoing abuse threatens her health regardless of pregnancy timing, and delay abandons the safety assessment the disclosure requires.
whyWrongByChoice.C: A positive disclosure requires action now — safety assessment and referral — not deferred written materials.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Absolute confidentiality cannot be promised; clinicians must comply with mandatory reporting requirements under state law.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bringing the abusive partner into the response is not part of the described intervention, which centers on the patient's safety and resources.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 24-year-old nulliparous woman requests permanent sterilization after counseling that presents all appropriate contraceptive options without bias and corrects her misconceptions. Which of the following must the provider verify before proceeding with this method?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That her decision is voluntary and free from coercion

choices.label: B
choices.text: That her partner has agreed to the procedure in writing

choices.label: C
choices.text: That she has already had at least one child

choices.label: D
choices.text: That she has completed a formal psychiatric evaluation

choices.label: E
choices.text: That she has first tried a long-acting reversible method

explanation.summary: For long-acting and permanent contraceptive methods, providers must verify that decisions are voluntary and free from coercion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Quality counseling involves ensuring informed consent and choice: presenting options without bias, correcting misconceptions, confirming understanding, and supporting the right to change methods. Particularly for long-acting and permanent methods, providers must verify that the decision is voluntary and free from coercion.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Partner consent is not a requirement; the counseling framework centers on the patient's own informed, voluntary choice.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Parity is not a prerequisite; reproductive autonomy includes nulliparous patients choosing permanent methods.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Psychiatric evaluation is not a condition for sterilization; the requirement is verification of voluntary, uncoerced consent.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A trial of another method is not required; counseling presents all appropriate options and supports the patient's choice among them.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A community health program is cataloging individual-level barriers that limit the reach of family planning services. Fear of side effects is reported as a reason for nonuse by approximately what proportion of females who are not using contraception?

explanation.summary: Fear of side effects is reported by approximately 40% of females not using contraception.
explanation.whyCorrect: Individual barriers to family planning services include limited knowledge about fertility and contraception, concerns about future fertility, partner opposition, and fear of side effects, which is reported by approximately 40% of females not using contraception. Recognizing these barriers helps programs target education and counseling.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 5% substantially understates how commonly fear of side effects is reported among nonusers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 10% is well below the stated figure of approximately 40%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 20% is only half of the approximately 40% of nonusers who report this fear.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 75% overstates the proportion; the figure given is approximately 40%.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A healthy 28-year-old woman and her female partner come to the office to discuss having a child; the patient plans to carry the pregnancy. Her menstrual cycles are regular, and she has no risk factors for infertility. Which of the following best describes the recommended timing of fertility evaluation and treatment for this couple?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deferral of any evaluation until the patient reaches 35 years of age

choices.label: B
choices.text: Evaluation limited to the partner who will not carry the pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Initiation earlier than the standard 12 months of attempted conception

choices.label: D
choices.text: Initiation only after 12 months of unsuccessful insemination attempts

choices.label: E
choices.text: No evaluation, because infertility cannot be defined for this couple

explanation.summary: Evaluation and treatment are initiated earlier than 12 months in nonheterosexual partnerships.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although infertility is defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of regular, unprotected intercourse, earlier initiation of evaluation and treatment is recommended when risk factors exist, when the female partner is 35 or older, and in the setting of nonheterosexual partnerships. This couple therefore should not be held to the 12-month standard.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Age 35 is a separate criterion for earlier evaluation, not a threshold this couple must reach before care begins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The partner planning to carry the pregnancy is central to the evaluation; restricting workup to the other partner makes no sense here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Waiting a full 12 months applies the standard heterosexual criterion; nonheterosexual partnerships are an explicit indication for earlier initiation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nonheterosexual partnerships are specifically named in the evaluation-timing recommendations, so evaluation is clearly available to them.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man is evaluated for infertility after 14 months of unprotected intercourse with his wife. Semen analysis shows a low sperm concentration. He reports self-administering intramuscular testosterone obtained at his gym for the past 2 years, drinking one cup of coffee daily, running recreationally, and taking a daily multivitamin; he fractured an ankle at age 20. Which of the following aspects of his history most likely contributes to his infertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daily caffeine intake

choices.label: B
choices.text: Daily multivitamin use

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous testosterone use

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recreational running

choices.label: E
choices.text: Remote ankle fracture

explanation.summary: Medication use, including exogenous testosterone, is a key element of the male infertility history and a contributor to impaired sperm production.
explanation.whyCorrect: The male infertility history specifically targets medication use, including exogenous testosterone, along with environmental or toxin exposures, tobacco and cannabis use, childhood illnesses such as mumps or cryptorchidism, sexual dysfunction, and sexually transmitted infections. His 2 years of intramuscular testosterone is the historical feature that fits this framework and best explains his low sperm concentration.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Caffeine is not among the exposures the male infertility history targets; tobacco and cannabis are the substances specifically sought.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A daily multivitamin is not an exposure implicated in male infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Recreational exercise is not listed as a contributor to male factor infertility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A remote orthopedic injury has no bearing on the reproductive history; relevant childhood illnesses are conditions such as mumps and cryptorchidism.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man undergoing infertility evaluation has a physical examination showing a normal penis and normal-sized testes, but the vas deferens is not palpable on either side. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Empiric exogenous testosterone therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genetic testing for cystic fibrosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Genetic testing for Y chromosome microdeletion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Karyotype analysis of both partners

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum heavy metal concentration measurement

explanation.summary: Absence of the vas deferens on physical examination should prompt cystic fibrosis testing.
explanation.whyCorrect: The male infertility physical examination includes body mass index, penile and testicular assessment, and evaluation for absence of the vas deferens, a finding that should specifically prompt cystic fibrosis testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Exogenous testosterone is a medication exposure sought in the history as a contributor to infertility, not a treatment for it.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Y chromosome microdeletion testing is triggered by azoospermia on semen analysis, not by the examination finding of an absent vas deferens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Karyotyping of the couple is not the response linked to this examination finding; the finding points specifically to cystic fibrosis testing.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Heavy metals are an environmental exposure explored in the history, not a test prompted by an absent vas deferens.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man provides a semen sample as part of an infertility evaluation. The analysis shows a sperm concentration slightly below the reference range with normal total count, motility, morphology, volume, and pH. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Diagnose male factor infertility based on this result

choices.label: B
choices.text: Order genetic testing for Y chromosome microdeletion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Proceed directly to intrauterine insemination

choices.label: D
choices.text: Repeat the semen analysis at least one month later

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the semen analysis later this week

explanation.summary: Because semen parameters vary substantially between ejaculates, an abnormal first analysis should be followed by a second analysis ideally at least one month later.
explanation.whyCorrect: Semen parameters are highly variable biological measures that may differ substantially from ejaculate to ejaculate, so at least two analyses, ideally obtained at least one month apart, are important — especially when the first shows abnormal parameters. A single mildly abnormal parameter is also of limited significance given the substantial overlap between fertile and infertile men.

whyWrongByChoice.A: No single parameter is truly diagnostic of infertility on its own; the clinical significance rises when multiple abnormalities coexist, and confirmation on repeat testing is needed first.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Y chromosome microdeletion testing is prompted by azoospermia, not by a mildly low concentration on one analysis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Jumping to treatment before confirming the finding on a properly spaced repeat analysis skips the indicated evaluation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Repeating within the same week does not satisfy the recommended spacing of at least one month between analyses.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 33-year-old man undergoing infertility evaluation has a semen analysis showing normal sperm concentration, normal morphology, and normal ejaculate volume, but a markedly reduced percentage of motile sperm. Which of the following terms describes this abnormality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Asthenozoospermia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azoospermia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normozoospermia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oligozoospermia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teratozoospermia

explanation.summary: Asthenozoospermia is reduced sperm motility, one of the most common semen analysis abnormalities.
explanation.whyCorrect: The most common abnormalities identified on semen analysis are low sperm concentration (oligozoospermia), reduced motility (asthenozoospermia), and abnormal morphology (teratozoospermia). Isolated reduction in the percentage of motile sperm is asthenozoospermia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Azoospermia is the complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate, not reduced motility of present sperm.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The sample is not normal; the motile fraction is markedly reduced.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Oligozoospermia is low sperm concentration, which is normal in this sample.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Teratozoospermia refers to abnormal morphology, which is normal here.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman is undergoing an initial infertility workup. After the history, physical examination, and laboratory studies, the physician considers pelvic ultrasonography and hysterosalpingography. Which of the following best describes the recommended approach to imaging in this evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Defer imaging until six cycles of ovulation induction have failed

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain both studies routinely in every female infertility evaluation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Order imaging only when all laboratory results return abnormal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reserve imaging for patients who are 35 years of age or older

choices.label: E
choices.text: Select imaging guided by the history and physical examination findings

explanation.summary: The decision to perform imaging in the female infertility workup should be guided by the history and physical examination, targeting pathology or modifiable conditions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pelvic ultrasonography and hysterosalpingography are often performed during the initial workup, but the decision to image should be guided by the history and physical examination. Imaging that focuses on pathology or modifiable conditions is higher yield than routine imaging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Imaging belongs to the initial diagnostic workup when indicated; it is not contingent on failed ovulation induction cycles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Routine imaging of every patient is specifically identified as lower yield than imaging directed at suspected pathology.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Laboratory results are not the gatekeeper for imaging; the history and examination guide the decision.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Age 35 changes when evaluation begins, not whether imaging is permitted within it.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman with anovulatory infertility is deciding between letrozole and clomiphene citrate for ovulation induction. Compared with letrozole, which of the following adverse effects is more characteristic of clomiphene?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Episodic dizziness and vertigo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gradual weight gain over time

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intermittent frontal headache

choices.label: D
choices.text: Persistent daytime fatigue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transient visual symptoms

explanation.summary: Rare visual symptoms are classically associated with clomiphene, whereas fatigue, dizziness, and headache are more typical of letrozole.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clomiphene more classically causes hot flashes, mood changes, breast tenderness, nausea, ovarian cysts with pelvic discomfort, and rare visual symptoms, and it can exert antiestrogenic effects on cervical mucus and the endometrium. Letrozole is instead commonly associated with fatigue, dizziness, headache, and hot flashes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dizziness is associated with letrozole rather than clomiphene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Weight gain is not described as an adverse effect of either agent.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Headache belongs to letrozole's adverse-effect profile in this comparison.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fatigue is listed among letrozole's common adverse effects, not clomiphene's classic profile.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with anovulatory infertility has completed six cycles of letrozole with documented ovulation in each cycle but has not conceived. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observation with unassisted attempts for another 12 months

choices.label: B
choices.text: Permanent discontinuation of all fertility treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Referral to a reproductive endocrinologist

choices.label: D
choices.text: Six additional cycles of letrozole at a higher dose

choices.label: E
choices.text: Switching to clomiphene citrate for six more cycles

explanation.summary: If pregnancy is not achieved after six cycles of ovulation induction, referral to an infertility specialist is recommended.
explanation.whyCorrect: When pregnancy is not achieved after six cycles of ovulation induction, referral to an infertility specialist is recommended. That next phase often includes assisted reproductive technology such as intrauterine insemination or in vitro fertilization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: She has been ovulating on treatment without conceiving; passive observation delays the specialist referral that is indicated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stopping treatment altogether abandons effective next options such as IUI and IVF that a specialist can offer.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Extending the same oral agent past six unsuccessful cycles is not the recommended course; the threshold for referral has been reached.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rotating to the other oral ovulation induction agent for another six cycles is not the described pathway after six failed cycles.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman with infertility asks about her likelihood of success with in vitro fertilization using her own oocytes. Which of the following is the approximate live birth rate per embryo transfer for females older than 43 years?

explanation.summary: IVF live birth rates decline from approximately 48.5% per embryo transfer for females under 35 to approximately 11.0% for females over 43.
explanation.whyCorrect: IVF is the most effective treatment for nearly all causes of infertility, but success is strongly age-dependent: live birth rates are approximately 48.5% per embryo transfer for females younger than 35 and decline to approximately 11.0% for females older than 43. At 44, this patient falls in the lower bracket.

whyWrongByChoice.B: 25% does not correspond to the cited rate for her age group; the figure for females over 43 is about 11%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Approximately 39% is the live birth rate per cycle with donor oocytes, not autologous IVF at her age.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Approximately 48.5% is the per-transfer live birth rate for females younger than 35, not older than 43.
whyWrongByChoice.E: 60% exceeds even the youngest group's per-transfer live birth rate.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 43-year-old woman with diminished ovarian reserve is counseled about proceeding with donor oocytes. She asks why pregnancy rates with donated oocytes are among the highest observed in assisted reproduction. Which of the following best explains this observation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Donated oocytes are uniformly free of all chromosomal abnormalities

choices.label: B
choices.text: Donated oocytes implant independently of the recipient's endometrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Donor cycles routinely involve the transfer of several embryos at once

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oocyte quality reflects the young donor's age rather than the recipient's

choices.label: E
choices.text: Recipients of donated oocytes do not require embryo transfer procedures

explanation.summary: Donor-oocyte pregnancy rates are among the highest in assisted reproduction because oocyte quality reflects the young donor's age rather than the recipient's.
explanation.whyCorrect: Donor oocytes or sperm may be considered when a partner has severe defects in gamete quality or quantity or a severe genetic condition. Pregnancy rates following oocyte donation are among the highest observed in assisted reproduction because the oocyte quality reflects the young donor's age rather than the recipient's, with live birth rates of approximately 39% per cycle.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Donation does not guarantee chromosomally normal oocytes; the advantage described is the donor's young age.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Implantation still depends on the recipient's uterus; the cited advantage concerns oocyte quality, not endometrium-independent implantation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Multiple-embryo transfer is not the stated reason for the high success of oocyte donation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Embryo transfer remains part of the process; donation changes the oocyte source, not the need for transfer.

questions.topicName: Family Planning, Preconception Care and Infertility

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus reports 1 year of erections insufficient for intercourse despite intact desire. He also notes fewer morning erections. Oral first-line therapy is prescribed. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this medication?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Agonism of central melanocortin receptors

choices.label: B
choices.text: Blockade of neuronal sodium channel conduction

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct stimulation of nitric oxide synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of serotonin reuptake at spinal synapses

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibition of the enzyme that degrades cGMP

explanation.summary: PDE5 inhibitors are first-line for erectile dysfunction and work by blocking cGMP breakdown.
explanation.whyCorrect: First-line treatment for erectile dysfunction is an oral PDE5 inhibitor (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil). PDE5 normally metabolizes cGMP; inhibiting it prolongs NO-mediated cavernosal smooth muscle relaxation, arterial inflow, and venous trapping, enhancing the erectile response.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Melanocortin receptor agonism is the mechanism of bremelanotide, used for female sexual interest/arousal disorder, not erectile dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Sodium channel blockade describes local anesthetics such as lidocaine, used topically for premature ejaculation or penetration-related pain.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PDE5 inhibitors do not generate nitric oxide; they preserve cGMP downstream, which is why benefit requires some retained capacity to produce endothelial and neurogenic NO.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Increased serotonergic signaling (SSRIs) inhibits arousal reflexes and delays ejaculation; it treats premature ejaculation and can cause erectile dysfunction.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man sustains a complete spinal cord transection at the T4 level in a motorcycle collision. Several months later, he is still able to achieve erections with direct genital stimulation. Which of the following pathways most likely mediates this preserved response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cortical arousal centers via descending spinal tracts

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypothalamic nuclei via brainstem autonomic relays

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sacral parasympathetic neurons via the pelvic splanchnic nerves

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatic motor neurons via the pudendal nerve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons via the hypogastric nerve

explanation.summary: Reflexogenic erections are mediated by a sacral (S2-S4) parasympathetic reflex arc that does not require input from the brain.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sacral parasympathetic neurons (S2-S4) mediate reflexogenic arousal from direct genital stimulation, controlling vasodilation and engorgement of erectile tissue via the pelvic splanchnic nerves. Because this reflex arc is entirely below a T4 lesion, males with severed spinal cords can still achieve erections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Descending cortical input is interrupted by a complete T4 transection, so brain-initiated (psychogenic) pathways cannot explain the preserved response.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypothalamic and brainstem pathways also require intact descending spinal connections, which a complete T4 lesion eliminates.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Somatic motor neurons via the pudendal nerve drive rhythmic bulbocavernosus and ischiocavernosus contractions during orgasm and expulsion, not erection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons (T11-L2) mediate psychogenic arousal and the emission phase of ejaculation, not the reflex erection from genital touch.

questions.stem: During the male sexual response, sperm move from the epididymis through the ductus deferens, and the prostate and seminal vesicles contract to push their contents into the bulb of the urethra, after which ejaculation can no longer be voluntarily stopped. Which of the following controls this phase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inhibitory GABAergic outflow from brainstem nuclei

choices.label: B
choices.text: Nonadrenergic-noncholinergic nerve terminal signaling

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sacral parasympathetic outflow through pelvic splanchnic nerves

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatic motor outflow through the pudendal nerve

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sympathetic outflow from thoracolumbar spinal segments

explanation.summary: Emission is under sympathetic control from thoracolumbar (T11-L2) neurons traveling via the hypogastric nerve.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sympathetic stimulation causes the ductus deferens, prostate, and seminal vesicles to contract, pushing contents into the urethral bulb. Thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons (T11-L2) control the emission phase of ejaculation, with efferent fibers in the hypogastric nerve.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GABA provides inhibition in brain and spinal circuits; it dampens rather than executes the emission reflex.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NANC terminals release nitric oxide for smooth muscle relaxation and erection, the opposite of the contractile events of emission.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Parasympathetic stimulation increases glandular secretions during excitement and plateau and mediates erection; it does not drive emission.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The pudendal nerve carries somatic fibers for the expulsion phase, the rhythmic ischiocavernosus and bulbocavernosus contractions that expel semen.

questions.stem: Researchers studying the human sexual response want a reliable neuroendocrine marker that orgasm has occurred in study participants of either sex. A blood level of which of the following hormones is best suited for this purpose?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oxytocin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progesterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone

explanation.summary: Prolactin rises substantially after orgasm in both sexes and stays elevated for over an hour, making it a reliable orgasm marker.
explanation.whyCorrect: Prolactin demonstrates a substantial, long-lasting increase following orgasm in both males and females, rising immediately and remaining elevated for 60 or more minutes. This sustained rise makes it a reliable neuroendocrine marker of orgasm.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol positively predicts sexual desire across the cycle in naturally cycling females; it is not a post-orgasm marker.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Oxytocin does increase acutely after orgasm, but its changes are less consistent and less sustained than prolactin elevations.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Progesterone negatively predicts sexual desire in naturally cycling females and does not mark the occurrence of orgasm.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone supports desire, arousal, and erectile function but is not described as spiking reliably after orgasm.

questions.stem: A study tracks daily hormone levels and self-reported sexual desire in healthy, naturally cycling women who are not using hormonal contraception. Based on the known hormonal influences on female sexual function, which pattern of results is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Desire falls with both higher estradiol and higher progesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: Desire rises with both higher estradiol and higher progesterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Desire rises with higher estradiol and falls with higher progesterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Desire rises with higher progesterone and falls with higher estradiol

choices.label: E
choices.text: Desire tracks prolactin levels and ignores ovarian steroids

explanation.summary: In naturally cycling females, estradiol positively predicts sexual desire while progesterone negatively predicts it.
explanation.whyCorrect: In naturally cycling females, estradiol positively predicts sexual desire and progesterone negatively predicts sexual desire, so desire should be highest when estradiol is high and progesterone is low.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Estradiol positively predicts desire, so desire should not fall as estradiol rises.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Progesterone negatively predicts desire, so desire should not rise with rising progesterone.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This reverses both relationships: progesterone is the negative predictor and estradiol the positive one.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Prolactin is a post-orgasm marker; ovarian steroids, not prolactin, are the predictors of cycling desire described.

questions.stem: During penile erection, intracavernosal pressure rises to approximate systolic blood pressure even before the ischiocavernosus muscles contract. Which of the following mechanisms is most responsible for trapping blood within the corpora cavernosa at this stage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Closure of the bladder neck by sympathetic stimulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compression of the subtunical venous plexus against the tunica albuginea

choices.label: C
choices.text: Constriction of cavernosal arteries reducing arterial inflow

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contraction of trabecular smooth muscle within the sinusoids

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thickening and tightening of the scrotum around the testes

explanation.summary: The veno-occlusive mechanism traps blood when expanding sinusoids compress subtunical veins against the rigid tunica albuginea.
explanation.whyCorrect: As the erectile bodies engorge, expanded sinusoids compress the subtunical venous plexus against the rigid tunica albuginea, restricting venous outflow and raising intracavernosal pressure to approximately systolic pressure. Ischiocavernosus contraction under pudendal control then pushes pressure above systolic for full rigidity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bladder neck closure occurs during ejaculation to prevent semen from mixing with urine; it does not trap blood in the corpora.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Erection depends on increased arterial inflow through dilated arteries; arterial constriction would oppose erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Erection requires relaxation, not contraction, of trabecular smooth muscle so arterial blood can fill the sinusoidal spaces.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Scrotal thickening and testicular elevation are plateau-phase changes and do not restrict penile venous outflow.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman asks her physician about a small volume of thick, milky fluid she sometimes releases at orgasm, which she distinguishes from her usual lubrication during arousal. This fluid most likely originates from which of the following structures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bulbourethral gland homologue secreting mucus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clitoral corpora cavernosa

choices.label: C
choices.text: Paraurethral (Skene's) glands

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uterine smooth muscle glands

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vaginal capillary transudation

explanation.summary: True female ejaculate is a small volume of thick, milky, PSA-containing fluid from the paraurethral (Skene's) glands.
explanation.whyCorrect: True female ejaculation originates from the paraurethral (Skene's) glands, the embryologic homologue of the male prostate. The fluid is a few milliliters of thick, milky secretion containing prostate-specific antigen and prostatic acid phosphatase, and may protect the urethra from microbes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Skene's glands are the homologue of the prostate, not of the bulbourethral glands, and the fluid is milky and PSA-rich rather than lubricating mucus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The clitoral corpora cavernosa are erectile vascular tissue that engorges; they are not secretory glands.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The uterus contracts during orgasm but is not the source of the milky ejaculate described.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal lubrication is a neurogenic plasma transudate driven by capillary pressure during vasocongestion; it is distinctly different from female ejaculation.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman reports that for the past 8 months she has had no interest in sexual activity, no erotic thoughts, no excitement or pleasure during encounters, and no arousal in response to cues she previously found stimulating. She is tearful and says the change is straining her marriage. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A daily trial of a serotonergic antidepressant such as an SSRI

choices.label: B
choices.text: Daily oral flibanserin taken at bedtime each night

choices.label: C
choices.text: Off-label transdermal testosterone replacement therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Psychological interventions such as CBT and couples therapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Subcutaneous bremelanotide before anticipated sexual activity

explanation.summary: Female sexual interest/arousal disorder is treated first with psychological interventions; medications are second options.
explanation.whyCorrect: This patient meets criteria for FSIAD: at least 3 of the 6 indicators are absent for at least 6 months with clinically significant distress. Psychological interventions, including CBT, mindfulness-based therapy, and couples or sex therapy, are first line for FSIAD.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SSRIs increase serotonergic signaling, which inhibits arousal reflexes; they cause rather than treat low desire and arousal.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Flibanserin, which is thought to alter central serotonergic signaling, is a medication option but not first-line therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Testosterone is off-label in the US, with the strongest evidence limited to carefully selected postmenopausal patients, and is not first line.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Bremelanotide, a melanocortin receptor agonist, is likewise a medication option rather than the initial treatment.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman reports 9 months of marked vulvar pain with attempted vaginal penetration, intense anxiety in anticipation of intercourse, and involuntary tightening of the muscles around the vaginal opening. The symptoms cause significant distress. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An SNRI for pain modulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Daily oral gabapentin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pelvic floor physical therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Topical local anesthetic before intercourse

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical vaginal estrogen

explanation.summary: Genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder is treated first with pelvic floor physical therapy.
explanation.whyCorrect: She meets criteria for GPPPD, the DSM-5 diagnosis combining dyspareunia and vaginismus: over 6 months of penetration difficulty, pelvic pain, fear or anxiety about pain, and pelvic floor tensing with distress. Pelvic floor physical therapy is first line because it directly targets the neuromuscular dysfunction with biofeedback, manual therapy, relaxation training, and graded dilation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: SNRIs can reduce centralized or neuropathic pelvic pain but are a medication option rather than first-line management.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Gabapentin, which dampens neuronal excitability via voltage-activated calcium channels, is an etiology-dependent medication option, not initial therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Local anesthetics reduce peripheral pain signaling during penetration but do not address the underlying pelvic floor dysfunction and are not first line.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal estrogen is most useful for hypoestrogenic or atrophy-related dyspareunia, which this young patient's presentation does not suggest.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is distressed because he consistently ejaculates within about a minute of penetration and cannot delay it, which is straining his relationship. Along with behavioral techniques, pharmacotherapy is planned. Which of the following best explains why the first-line drug class is effective for this condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enhanced dopaminergic signaling heightens sexual desire

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased serotonergic signaling inhibits the ejaculatory reflex

choices.label: C
choices.text: Melanocortin receptor agonism modulates central arousal pathways

choices.label: D
choices.text: Preserved cGMP prolongs cavernosal smooth muscle relaxation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced catecholamine reuptake increases noradrenergic tone

explanation.summary: SSRIs are first-line for premature ejaculation because serotonin inhibits the ejaculatory reflex and delays ejaculation.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is premature ejaculation: ejaculation within about 1 minute of penetration with inability to delay it and significant distress. SSRIs, including on-demand dapoxetine, are first-line medications because increased serotonergic signaling inhibits the ejaculatory reflex; topical anesthetics are also first line, and combination therapy beats monotherapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dopamine facilitates desire and arousal; enhancing it would not delay ejaculation and is not the treatment mechanism here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Melanocortin agonism describes bremelanotide, used for female sexual interest/arousal disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.D: cGMP preservation is the PDE5 inhibitor mechanism used for erectile dysfunction, not for delaying ejaculation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibition describes bupropion, used to improve desire or counter SSRI-related dysfunction, not to delay ejaculation.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man with sickle cell disease presents to the emergency department with a painful erection that has lasted 6 hours. He recently started taking trazodone for insomnia. In addition to corporal aspiration, which of the following is the most appropriate next step in treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collagenase injection into the corpora

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intracavernosal phenylephrine injection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation until detumescence occurs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Oral sildenafil administration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical lidocaine application

explanation.summary: Ischemic priapism is a medical emergency treated with corporal aspiration and intracavernosal phenylephrine.
explanation.whyCorrect: A sustained, painful erection lasting longer than 4 hours is priapism, which is associated with sickle cell disease and with medications, trazodone being among the most common. Ischemic priapism requires immediate treatment to prevent permanent tissue damage and erectile dysfunction; common treatments are corporal aspiration to drain excess blood and intracavernosal phenylephrine to open veins.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Collagenase is used to break down the fibrous plaques of Peyronie disease, not to treat priapism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ischemic priapism is a medical emergency; observation risks permanent tissue damage and erectile dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sildenafil prolongs smooth muscle relaxation and enhances erection, which would worsen rather than relieve priapism.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Topical lidocaine reduces sensory pain signaling but does nothing to relieve the trapped blood causing ischemia.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old man with long-standing diabetes mellitus is evaluated for infertility. He reports normal orgasms but says little or no semen comes out, and his urine appears cloudy after intercourse. Which of the following is the most likely underlying mechanism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A lax sphincter at the base of the bladder

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the seminal vesicles to produce fructose

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fibrous plaques surrounding the corpora cavernosa

choices.label: D
choices.text: Obstruction of the ductus deferens by scarring

choices.label: E
choices.text: Weakness of the bulbocavernosus and ischiocavernosus muscles

explanation.summary: Retrograde ejaculation, a cause of male infertility, usually results from a lax bladder-neck sphincter, commonly from diabetes, pelvic surgery, or autonomic dysfunction.
explanation.whyCorrect: During normal ejaculation the bladder neck closes tightly so semen cannot mix with urine. Retrograde ejaculation occurs when this sphincter is lax, letting semen pass backward into the bladder; common causes include diabetes mellitus, prostate or other pelvic surgery, autonomic nerve dysfunction, and certain antidepressants and antipsychotics.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Seminal vesicle fructose supplies sperm energy; its absence would not send semen backward into the bladder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fibrous plaques around the corpora cavernosa cause Peyronie disease, with penile curvature and painful erections, not absent antegrade semen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ductal obstruction is not the mechanism described for this diabetes-associated pattern of orgasm with semen appearing in the urine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Weak striated pelvic muscles would impair expulsion force but would not divert semen into the bladder or cloud the post-coital urine.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man and his 27-year-old wife ask their physician why she can experience several orgasms in quick succession during intercourse, whereas after he ejaculates he is unable to respond to further sexual stimulation for some time. Which of the following best explains his experience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A normal refractory period of the male response

choices.label: B
choices.text: A pathologic postorgasmic decline in testosterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Early-onset erectile dysfunction

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of the resolution phase to occur

choices.label: E
choices.text: Retrograde passage of semen into the bladder

explanation.summary: Males have a refractory period after orgasm during which they cannot respond to sexual stimulation; females can cycle again quickly and achieve multiple orgasms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Males experience a refractory period of variable duration, usually minutes to hours, during which they are unable to respond to sexual stimulation. In females, successive response cycles can follow quickly, which is why multiple orgasms are possible. This asymmetry is a normal feature of the sexual response patterns, not a disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone supports male desire, arousal, and erectile function, but the postorgasmic refractory period is not described as a pathologic testosterone decline.
whyWrongByChoice.C: He attains erection and ejaculates normally; a temporary inability to respond after orgasm is a normal refractory period, not persistent inability to attain and maintain an erection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Resolution, the return to the pre-arousal state with reversal of vasocongestion and muscle tension, is occurring normally; it does not represent a failure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Retrograde ejaculation sends semen backward into the bladder and causes infertility with cloudy post-coital urine; it does not explain a normal postorgasmic pause.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman tells her physician she is worried because she rarely feels spontaneous sexual desire before intimacy begins, although once sexual activity starts she becomes interested, aroused, and satisfied, and she reports no distress about her sexual life. Based on the proposed models of the female sexual response, which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Desire may follow arousal rather than precede it in females

choices.label: B
choices.text: Her pattern indicates female orgasmic disorder

choices.label: C
choices.text: Her pattern indicates female sexual interest/arousal disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sexual desire must precede arousal for a normal response

choices.label: E
choices.text: The female response always follows a fixed linear sequence

explanation.summary: The female sexual response can be nonlinear or circular, and desire may follow arousal rather than precede it.
explanation.whyCorrect: The stages of the sexual response cycle can be sequential (most commonly in males) or nonlinear with overlapping phases or variable order. A more complex circular pattern has been proposed for the female response, and desire may follow arousal rather than precede it, especially in females. Her pattern is a normal variation.

whyWrongByChoice.B: She reports satisfaction and no distress; female orgasmic disorder involves absent, delayed, or reduced orgasm in most encounters with significant distress.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSIAD requires absence or reduction of at least 3 of 6 indicators for at least 6 months with clinically significant distress; she is aroused, interested once activity begins, and not distressed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Desire may follow arousal rather than precede it; a fixed desire-first requirement contradicts the circular model of female response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The sequential pattern is most common in males; the female response can be nonlinear with overlapping phases or variable order.

questions.stem: During a monitored study of the male sexual response, a participant's testicles are noted to engorge, swelling by 50% or more, while the scrotum thickens and tightens, drawing the testicles closer to the body. These findings are characteristic of which stage of the sexual response cycle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Excitement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Orgasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Plateau

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refractory period

choices.label: E
choices.text: Resolution

explanation.summary: The plateau stage features marked testicular engorgement (50% or more) with scrotal thickening and tightening that elevates the testicles.
explanation.whyCorrect: During the plateau stage, the testicles undergo significant engorgement, swelling by 50% or more due to increased blood flow, while the scrotum simultaneously thickens and tightens, moving the testicles closer to the body. This phase is not well understood in females.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Excitement begins with physical or psychologic stimulation and brings increased heart rate, breathing, flushed skin, erection, and only initial testicular swelling, not the marked engorgement and scrotal tightening described.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Orgasm is the climax of involuntary muscle contractions that forces semen out of the urethra; it is not defined by testicular engorgement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The refractory period follows orgasm in males, when they cannot respond to further stimulation; it is not marked by testicular swelling.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Resolution is the return to the pre-arousal state with reversal of vasocongestion and muscle tension, the opposite of progressive engorgement.

questions.stem: A researcher is characterizing the facilitatory neurotransmitters that modulate the human sexual response. According to this framework, dopamine mediates sexual desire and arousal through the release of which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: GABA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glutamate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Oxytocin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prolactin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serotonin

explanation.summary: Dopamine is a facilitatory neurotransmitter that mediates sexual desire and arousal through oxytocin release.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the facilitatory neurotransmitters of the sexual response, dopamine mediates sexual desire and arousal through oxytocin release. Oxytocin itself is released during arousal and orgasm and mediates pleasure, euphoria, and physiological responses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: GABA is inhibitory, providing inhibition in brain and spinal cord circuits, and is not the downstream mediator of dopamine's facilitation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glutamate provides excitatory neurotransmission in its own right but is not described as the mediator through which dopamine drives desire and arousal.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prolactin rises after orgasm and serves as a neuroendocrine marker of orgasm; it is not the effector of dopamine-driven desire and arousal.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serotonin is an inhibitory neurotransmitter that inhibits genital arousal reflexes and delays ejaculation; dopamine does not act by releasing it.

questions.stem: In the peripheral mechanism of genital arousal, nitric oxide is the main neurotransmitter mediating penile and clitoral smooth muscle relaxation. Nitric oxide reaches the cavernosal smooth muscle from which two sources?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenergic sympathetic terminals and circulating platelets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cholinergic terminals and trabecular smooth muscle cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: NANC autonomic nerve terminals and vascular endothelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sensory afferent terminals and urethral gland epithelium

choices.label: E
choices.text: Somatic motor terminals and the tunica albuginea

explanation.summary: Nitric oxide is released from nonadrenergic-noncholinergic (NANC) autonomic nerve terminals and from the vascular endothelium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The main neurotransmitter mediating penile and clitoral smooth muscle relaxation is nitric oxide, released from two sources: nonadrenergic-noncholinergic (NANC) autonomic nerve terminals and the vascular endothelium. This dual neurogenic and endothelial supply is why PDE5 inhibitors only work when some capacity to generate endothelial and neurogenic NO is retained.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenergic sympathetic signaling drives emission and contraction of the ductus deferens, prostate, and seminal vesicles, not NO-mediated relaxation, and platelets are not a described NO source here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The NO-releasing autonomic terminals are specifically nonadrenergic-noncholinergic, and trabecular smooth muscle is the target of NO, not its source.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Sensory afferents in the pudendal nerve trigger the expulsion reflex as the urethra fills; neither they nor urethral gland epithelium are described sources of NO.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Somatic motor fibers in the pudendal nerve drive skeletal muscle contraction during expulsion, and the tunica albuginea is a fibroelastic covering, not a secretory source of NO.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man undergoes extensive retroperitoneal surgery during which the hypogastric nerves are damaged. Afterward, he no longer develops erections in response to erotic visual stimuli or mental imagery, although erections from direct genital stimulation are preserved. Dysfunction of which of the following neuronal populations best explains his deficit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Brainstem autonomic nuclei of the pons

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypothalamic nuclei of the medial preoptic area

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sacral parasympathetic neurons (S2-S4)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatic motor neurons (S2-S4) of Onuf nucleus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons (T11-L2)

explanation.summary: Psychogenic arousal is mediated by thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons (T11-L2) whose efferent fibers travel in the hypogastric nerve.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thoracolumbar sympathetic neurons (T11-L2) mediate psychogenic arousal from mental imagery and visual stimuli, and their efferent fibers travel via the hypogastric nerve. Damage to the hypogastric nerves therefore eliminates psychogenic arousal while leaving the sacral reflexogenic pathway intact, so erections from direct genital stimulation persist.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Brainstem nuclei participate centrally in coordinating arousal, but his lesion is peripheral, in the efferent hypogastric nerve fibers, not the brainstem.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hypothalamic nuclei likewise remain intact; the interrupted link is the peripheral sympathetic efferent pathway carrying psychogenic signals to the genitals.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Sacral parasympathetic neurons (S2-S4) mediate reflexogenic arousal via the pelvic splanchnic nerves; his preserved response to direct genital stimulation shows this pathway is intact.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Somatic motor neurons via the pudendal nerve control the rhythmic bulbocavernosus and ischiocavernosus contractions of orgasm and expulsion, not arousal from imagery.

questions.stem: As the urethra fills with semen during the male sexual response, sensory signals trigger rhythmic contractions of the ischiocavernosus and bulbocavernosus skeletal muscles at the base of the penis, expelling semen. The efferent fibers driving these contractions travel in which of the following nerves?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hypogastric nerve

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ilioinguinal nerve

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obturator nerve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pelvic splanchnic nerves

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pudendal nerve

explanation.summary: Somatic motor neurons (S2-S4) traveling via the pudendal nerve drive the rhythmic skeletal muscle contractions of the expulsion phase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Somatic motor neurons at S2-S4 control the rhythmic contractions of the bulbocavernosus and ischiocavernosus muscles during orgasm and the expulsion phase of ejaculation, and their efferent fibers travel via the pudendal nerve. The pudendal nerve also carries the sensory signals generated as the urethra fills with semen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The hypogastric nerve carries thoracolumbar sympathetic fibers for psychogenic arousal and the emission phase, which contracts the ductus deferens, prostate, and seminal vesicles.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The ilioinguinal nerve is not one of the described efferent pathways controlling genital responses in the sexual response.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The obturator nerve supplies the thigh and is not part of the neural control of ejaculation.
