Because progesterone can be given orally, transdermally, or via an intrauterine system, switching routes maintains endometrial protection while avoiding the oral formulation's sedating effect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Raising the estrogen dose increases unopposed endometrial stimulation, the very problem to be avoided.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Testosterone replacement is therapy for symptomatic hypogonadal males and has no role in endometrial protection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ospemifene is a SERM for dyspareunia from vulvovaginal atrophy, not a progestogen substitute.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Vaginal estrogen treats genitourinary symptoms and adds estrogen rather than opposing it at the endometrium.

questions.stem: An 82-year-old female with a history of stroke has disabling hot flashes and is prescribed oxybutynin. Which of the following pairs this drug's mechanism for hot flashes with the main limitation of its use at her age?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bypass of first-pass hepatic metabolism; unstable hormone levels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcium channel modulation; pronounced sedation at bedtime

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen agonism in vaginal tissue; stimulation of the endometrium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibition of sweat gland activity; anticholinergic side effects

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serotonin reuptake inhibition; efficacy below that of hormone therapy

explanation.summary: Oxybutynin reduces hot flashes by inhibiting sweat gland activity, but anticholinergic side effects limit its use in older females.
explanation.whyCorrect: Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic used primarily for overactive bladder that has shown efficacy for hot flashes, likely through inhibition of sweat gland activity. Its anticholinergic adverse effects limit its use in older females, which is the central consideration for a woman of 82.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bypassing first-pass metabolism describes transdermal estrogen, which actually yields more stable levels.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Calcium channel modulation with sedation describes gabapentin, which is often dosed at bedtime for that reason.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Vaginal estrogen agonism describes ospemifene, a SERM used for dyspareunia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Serotonin reuptake inhibition describes the SSRIs and SNRIs used for vasomotor symptoms, not oxybutynin.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female with vulvovaginal atrophy declines all hormonal treatment. She reports daily vaginal discomfort as well as friction and pain during intercourse. Which of the following best describes the roles of the nonhormonal products appropriate for her?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both products act as estrogen agonists confined to urogenital tissue

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both products reverse the underlying atrophic changes of the vaginal epithelium

choices.label: C
choices.text: Moisturizers improve hydration and elasticity; lubricants reduce friction during intercourse

choices.label: D
choices.text: Moisturizers lower vaginal pH; lubricants restore vaginal rugae and thickness

choices.label: E
choices.text: Moisturizers reduce friction during intercourse; lubricants improve hydration and elasticity

explanation.summary: Vaginal moisturizers improve hydration and elasticity, while lubricants reduce friction and discomfort during intercourse; neither reverses atrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: For genitourinary symptoms, vaginal moisturizers and lubricants provide symptomatic relief without hormonal effects: moisturizers improve vaginal hydration and elasticity, and lubricants reduce friction and discomfort during intercourse. Local vaginal estrogen is what more effectively treats the underlying atrophic changes when symptoms are moderate to severe or persist despite these measures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: These are nonhormonal products; tissue-selective estrogen agonism describes ospemifene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neither product reverses atrophy; that is the advantage of local vaginal estrogen therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neither product is described as restoring pH or rugae; those changes follow estrogen deficiency and respond to estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The roles are reversed; lubricants address intercourse-related friction and moisturizers address baseline hydration.

questions.stem: A 53-year-old female with moderate hot flashes asks whether over-the-counter plant-derived supplements with estrogen-like activity would let her avoid prescription treatment. Which of the following best describes the evidence for these agents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consistently superior to systemic hormone therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Contraindicated in any female with an intact uterus

choices.label: C
choices.text: Effective only for genitourinary symptoms

choices.label: D
choices.text: Equivalent to SSRIs in randomized trials

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mixed evidence, with modest effects at best

explanation.summary: Phytoestrogens have mixed evidence with modest effects at best for vasomotor symptoms.
explanation.whyCorrect: Phytoestrogens are plant-derived compounds with estrogen-like activity, and the evidence supporting them is mixed, with modest effects at best. They sit among the non-hormonal approaches of varying evidence quality, well below hormone therapy, which reduces hot flashes by 75-80%.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms; no supplement outperforms it.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Phytoestrogens are not listed as contraindicated by uterine status; that consideration applies to systemic estrogen therapy.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Phytoestrogens are discussed as an option for vasomotor symptoms, and moisturizers, lubricants, or local estrogen target genitourinary symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: SSRIs and SNRIs have demonstrated efficacy with roughly 40-60% reduction in hot flashes; phytoestrogen evidence is far weaker.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old female with mild hot flashes prefers to try nonpharmacologic measures first. Which of the following recommendations is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Avoid alcohol, caffeine, and spicy foods

choices.label: B
choices.text: Avoid weight-bearing exercise to limit sweating

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase caffeine intake in the evening

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restrict fluid intake in order to reduce night sweats

choices.label: E
choices.text: Take phytoestrogen supplements instead of exercising

explanation.summary: Lifestyle management of vasomotor symptoms includes exercise, weight management, smoking cessation, and avoiding triggers such as alcohol, caffeine, and spicy foods.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lifestyle modification for menopausal symptoms comprises regular exercise, weight management, smoking cessation, and avoidance of triggers including alcohol, caffeine, and spicy foods. These measures are reasonable first steps for mild symptoms and carry none of the risks of systemic therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Regular exercise is recommended; it also supports weight management and bone health after menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Caffeine is a recognized trigger to avoid, and evening intake would also worsen sleep disturbance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fluid restriction is not among the recommended measures and does not address hypothalamic thermoregulatory dysfunction.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exercise is a recommended measure, and phytoestrogens have mixed evidence with modest effects at best.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old male with advanced prostate cancer treated by medical castration reports fatigue, loss of muscle mass, reduced libido, and depressed mood. Compared with a 58-year-old male whose testosterone has drifted downward gradually since age 40, which of the following best characterizes this patient?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He has the typical age-related decline expected for his age

choices.label: B
choices.text: He has true andropause from loss of testicular function

choices.label: C
choices.text: He should be expected to progress through defined andropause stages

choices.label: D
choices.text: His decline is driven solely by sex hormone-binding globulin changes

choices.label: E
choices.text: His testosterone loss is confined to central hypothalamic mechanisms

explanation.summary: True andropause exists only in males who have lost testicular function through disease, injury, or castration for advanced prostate cancer.
explanation.whyCorrect: Andropause refers to age-related testosterone decline with bothersome symptoms, but true andropause exists only in males who have lost testicular function because of disease or accident, or who have undergone surgical or medical castration for advanced prostate cancer. This patient's castration places him in that category, unlike a peer undergoing the usual gradual decline.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The typical pattern is a gradual fall of about 1% per year after age 40, not the abrupt loss produced by castration.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Andropause is characterized by gradual onset and slow progression without defined stages, in contrast to menopause.
whyWrongByChoice.D: SHBG alterations make the fall in free testosterone more pronounced during normal aging, but they do not explain castration.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Age-related decline involves both central hypothalamic-pituitary and peripheral Leydig cell mechanisms, and his loss is at the testicular level.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old male with obesity, poorly controlled chronic illness, high occupational stress, and several chronic medications has a borderline-low testosterone level and mild fatigue. Which of the following best describes how these factors relate to his testosterone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They accelerate the age-related decline, which lifestyle measures can slow

choices.label: B
choices.text: They cause abrupt, permanent cessation of testicular testosterone output

choices.label: C
choices.text: They have no measurable effect on the rate of decline

choices.label: D
choices.text: They make testosterone replacement permanently contraindicated

choices.label: E
choices.text: They raise testosterone by increasing sex hormone-binding globulin

explanation.summary: The rate of testosterone decline is modified by chronic disease, obesity, stress, and medications, and can be slowed by diet, exercise, and mental activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: The rate of decline in testosterone varies and is affected by chronic disease, obesity, emotional stress, and medications. It can be slowed by managing lifestyle factors such as diet, physical exercise, and mental activity, making these the first target in a male like this one with borderline levels and mild symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Abrupt permanent loss of testicular output characterizes castration or testicular injury, not comorbidity.
whyWrongByChoice.C: These are precisely the factors described as altering the rate of decline.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Replacement therapy is available for males with symptoms or laboratory evidence of hypogonadism; these factors do not permanently bar it.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SHBG alterations accentuate the fall in free testosterone with age; comorbidity lowers rather than raises testosterone.

questions.stem: A 64-year-old male has a total testosterone level of 290 ng/dL discovered on a screening panel ordered for another reason. He reports normal libido, regular morning erections, good energy, normal mood, and stable muscle strength. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Start an SSRI to treat subclinical hypogonadal mood symptoms

choices.label: B
choices.text: Start GnRH agonist therapy to restore pulsatile gonadotropin release

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start intramuscular testosterone targeting a level above 900 ng/dL

choices.label: D
choices.text: Start transdermal testosterone to prevent future symptom development

choices.label: E
choices.text: Withhold testosterone therapy and address lifestyle factors with monitoring

explanation.summary: Many males with low testosterone are asymptomatic; replacement is for males with symptoms or laboratory evidence of hypogonadism, and lifestyle management can slow the decline.
explanation.whyCorrect: The threshold at which symptoms manifest varies, and many males with low testosterone levels are not symptomatic. Hormone replacement is offered to symptomatic males with hypogonadism, while the rate of decline can be slowed by managing diet, physical exercise, and mental activity, making observation with lifestyle measures appropriate here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: He has no mood symptoms, and SSRIs are used for vasomotor symptoms or depression, not for an asymptomatic low testosterone level.
whyWrongByChoice.B: GnRH agonist therapy is not a treatment for age-related testosterone decline; medical castration with such agents is what produces true andropause.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The therapeutic goal is a physiologic level of 400-700 ng/dL; supratherapeutic levels risk cardiovascular complications, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and suppressed spermatogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Treatment is directed at symptomatic hypogonadism, not at prophylaxis in an asymptomatic male.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman presents with irregular menses since menarche, worsening hirsutism of the chin and upper lip, and acne. Her BMI is 33 kg/m2. Pelvic ultrasound shows multiple peripheral ovarian follicles in a string-of-pearls pattern. Laboratory studies show an elevated free testosterone with a normal DHEA-S. Which of the following best explains her elevated free testosterone level?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal 21-hydroxylase deficiency shunting precursors to androgens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autonomous DHEA-S secretion from an adrenal neoplasm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decreased GnRH pulse frequency reducing FSH secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyperinsulinemia suppressing sex hormone-binding globulin production

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased hepatic synthesis of sex hormone-binding globulin

explanation.summary: In PCOS, insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia suppress SHBG, raising free testosterone.
explanation.whyCorrect: PCOS involves a self-reinforcing cycle in which increased GnRH pulse frequency drives LH-mediated ovarian androgen overproduction, while insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia further stimulate androgen synthesis and suppress SHBG. Lower SHBG leaves a larger fraction of testosterone unbound, so free testosterone rises.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia is screened for with 17-OHP and is an adrenal cause; her normal DHEA-S and classic PCOS picture point to an ovarian etiology.
whyWrongByChoice.B: An adrenal androgen source would produce an elevated DHEA-S, which is normal here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: PCOS features an increased, not decreased, GnRH pulse frequency, which favors LH-driven ovarian androgen production.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SHBG is suppressed, not increased, in PCOS; increased SHBG would lower, not raise, free testosterone.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presents with 4 months of rapidly progressive facial hair growth and deepening of her voice. Laboratory studies show a markedly elevated DHEA-S, a mildly elevated total testosterone, and a normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Which of the following is the most likely source of her androgen excess?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A tumor of the adrenal gland

choices.label: B
choices.text: An androgen-secreting ovarian tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia from 21-hydroxylase deficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH-driven ovarian overproduction in PCOS

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surreptitious use of danazol

explanation.summary: An elevated DHEA-S localizes androgen excess to an adrenal source.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the female hyperandrogenism workup, elevated DHEA-S suggests an adrenal source, while elevated testosterone with normal DHEA-S points to an ovarian etiology. Rapid virilization with a markedly elevated DHEA-S and normal 17-OHP therefore indicates an adrenal tumor, and adrenal CT imaging is pursued when DHEA-S is elevated.

whyWrongByChoice.B: An ovarian tumor such as a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor produces elevated testosterone with a normal DHEA-S.
whyWrongByChoice.C: 21-hydroxylase deficiency is screened for with 17-OHP, which is normal in this patient.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PCOS causes gradual hirsutism with irregular menses, not rapid virilization with a markedly elevated DHEA-S.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Exogenous agents like danazol would not produce a markedly elevated endogenous DHEA-S.

questions.stem: A 21-year-old woman is evaluated for hirsutism and irregular menses. As part of the initial laboratory workup for hyperandrogenism, which of the following tests screens for congenital adrenal hyperplasia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 17-hydroxyprogesterone

choices.label: B
choices.text: DHEA sulfate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Luteinizing hormone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sex hormone-binding globulin

explanation.summary: 17-OHP is the screening test for congenital adrenal hyperplasia in hyperandrogenic females.
explanation.whyCorrect: Initial labs for female hyperandrogenism include total and free testosterone, DHEA-S, and 17-hydroxyprogesterone. The 17-OHP is included specifically to screen for congenital adrenal hyperplasia, particularly 21-hydroxylase deficiency, in which this precursor accumulates.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DHEA-S helps localize excess to an adrenal versus ovarian source; it is not the CAH screen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Free testosterone confirms biochemical hyperandrogenism but does not identify CAH.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH helps assess the HPG axis but does not screen for an adrenal enzyme defect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SHBG affects the free testosterone fraction and is not a screening test for CAH.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old competitive bodybuilder presents with 1 year of infertility. Examination shows marked muscularity, truncal acne, and small, soft testes bilaterally. Laboratory studies show an elevated serum testosterone with low LH and low FSH. Which of the following best explains his infertility?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androgen receptor insensitivity in peripheral target tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deficient aromatization of testosterone to estradiol in adipose tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous androgen suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary testicular failure from prior mumps orchitis with tubular atrophy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolactin-mediated suppression of hypothalamic GnRH pulse release

explanation.summary: Exogenous androgens suppress the HPG axis, causing testicular atrophy and infertility despite high testosterone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Exogenous androgen use is the most prevalent cause of androgen excess in young men. It suppresses hypothalamic-pituitary output, lowering LH and FSH, which produces testicular atrophy (loss of FSH support) and infertility even though circulating testosterone is elevated.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgen insensitivity produces elevated testosterone with an elevated, not suppressed, LH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase deficiency causes skeletal abnormalities from estrogen deficiency; it does not explain suppressed gonadotropins with atrophic testes in a steroid user.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary testicular failure would show low testosterone with elevated LH and FSH from loss of negative feedback.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyperprolactinemia causes secondary hypogonadism with low testosterone, not elevated testosterone.

questions.stem: Laboratory evaluation of a patient with a disorder of androgen physiology shows an elevated serum testosterone together with an elevated LH. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androgen insensitivity syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exogenous androgen use

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypergonadotropic (primary) hypogonadism

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone-secreting tumor

explanation.summary: Elevated testosterone with elevated LH indicates androgen insensitivity syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: When target tissues cannot respond to androgens, negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary fails, so LH stays high and continues to drive testosterone production. The combination of high testosterone and high LH is therefore the signature of androgen insensitivity syndrome.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Exogenous androgens raise testosterone but suppress LH through intact negative feedback.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Primary hypogonadism shows low testosterone with elevated LH from gonadal failure.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Secondary hypogonadism shows low testosterone with low or inappropriately normal LH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A testosterone-secreting tumor also produces high testosterone with a suppressed LH.

questions.stem: A 17-year-old boy is evaluated for absent pubertal development. He has small testes, no facial or axillary hair, and reports that he has never been able to smell. Serum testosterone, LH, and FSH are all low. Which of the following best explains his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 47,XXY karyotype with primary testicular failure

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autosomal recessive deficiency of the aromatase enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failed migration of GnRH-producing neurons during fetal development

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ischemic testicular injury from remote testicular torsion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prolactin-secreting tumor compressing the pituitary stalk

explanation.summary: Kallmann syndrome pairs hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia due to failed GnRH neuron migration.
explanation.whyCorrect: Kallmann syndrome is a congenital form of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism caused by impaired migration of GnRH-producing neurons during fetal development. Delayed or absent puberty with a reduced or absent sense of smell distinguishes it from other causes of secondary hypogonadism, and the low LH and FSH confirm the central defect.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Klinefelter syndrome is primary hypogonadism, so LH and FSH would be elevated, and anosmia is not a feature.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase deficiency presents with tall stature, unfused epiphyses, and osteoporosis with elevated testosterone and gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Testicular torsion causes primary testicular failure with elevated gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hyperprolactinemia can cause secondary hypogonadism but does not explain lifelong anosmia.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man with confirmed symptomatic hypogonadism (two low morning testosterone levels with low LH and FSH) wishes to conceive a child with his partner within the next year. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Gonadotropin therapy with hCG

choices.label: B
choices.text: Intramuscular testosterone replacement therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Metformin for metabolic support

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spironolactone with dose titration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transdermal testosterone replacement therapy

explanation.summary: Men with hypogonadism who desire fertility should receive gonadotropin therapy, not testosterone replacement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Testosterone replacement therapy is contraindicated in men desiring fertility because it suppresses spermatogenesis. In these patients, gonadotropin therapy with hCG, with FSH added if needed, is preferred because it stimulates endogenous testosterone production and preserves fertility.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Intramuscular testosterone suppresses spermatogenesis and would undermine his fertility goal.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Metformin addresses insulin resistance in PCOS and has no role in treating male hypogonadism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spironolactone is an androgen receptor blocker used for hirsutism in females and would worsen androgen deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The route does not change the problem; transdermal testosterone also suppresses spermatogenesis.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man presents with a 3-month history of a tender, firm subareolar mass of the left breast consistent with true gynecomastia. He takes no medications and does not use anabolic steroids. Serum estradiol is elevated. In addition to LH, FSH, and testosterone levels, which of the following is the most appropriate next step to exclude a dangerous underlying cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal CT with serum cortisol measurement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Core needle biopsy of the breast tissue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Empiric anastrozole with follow-up examination

choices.label: D
choices.text: MRI of the pituitary with prolactin level

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum hCG and AFP with testicular ultrasound

explanation.summary: New gynecomastia with elevated estradiol in a young man requires hCG, AFP, and testicular ultrasound to exclude a germ cell tumor.
explanation.whyCorrect: In males with gynecomastia, hCG, alpha-fetoprotein, and testicular ultrasound are obtained to exclude a germ cell tumor. Recognizing gynecomastia as a potential sign of an underlying tumor, such as a Leydig cell or germ cell tumor of the testis, is a key clinical skill, and this evaluation takes priority in a young man with unexplained estrogen excess.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal imaging is pursued when elevated DHEA-S or cortisol suggests adrenal pathology, which has not been shown here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Breast biopsy evaluates the local tissue but does not identify the underlying source of estrogen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aromatase inhibitors treat persistent hyperestrogenism only after the root cause has been identified and addressed.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A pituitary workup does not address the estrogen-secreting testicular tumors that must be excluded first in this setting.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man treated with spironolactone develops bilateral painful breast enlargement. Serum estradiol and testosterone are within normal limits. Which of the following best explains his gynecomastia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct stimulation of estrogen receptors by the drug

choices.label: B
choices.text: hCG secretion from an occult germ cell tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired hepatic metabolism of circulating estrogens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased estradiol synthesis by the adrenal glands

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased peripheral aromatization in adipose tissue

explanation.summary: Spironolactone causes gynecomastia by stimulating estrogen receptors, not by raising estrogen levels.
explanation.whyCorrect: Spironolactone does not increase estrogen levels; it causes an estrogen-like effect. It blocks aldosterone and androgen receptors and also stimulates estrogen receptors, producing painful breast enlargement in women and gynecomastia in men, which fits his normal estradiol level.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A germ cell tumor would be suggested by an elevated hCG and abnormal hormone levels, not normal labs on a culprit drug.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Liver disease elevates estrogen levels by impairing their metabolism, which is not seen here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: There is no indication of an adrenal source, and his estradiol is not elevated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Obesity-related aromatization raises estradiol, but his estradiol is normal.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman with a BMI of 36 kg/m2 presents with vaginal bleeding 3 years after her last menstrual period. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Combined oral contraceptive pills for cycle control

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial biopsy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reassurance with routine annual follow-up

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum estradiol measurement repeated in 3 months

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transvaginal ultrasound deferred for 6 months

explanation.summary: Postmenopausal bleeding warrants urgent evaluation with endometrial biopsy for endometrial pathology.
explanation.whyCorrect: In postmenopausal women, any uterine bleeding warrants urgent evaluation for endometrial pathology, and endometrial biopsy is indicated for postmenopausal bleeding. Her obesity increases peripheral aromatization of androgens to estrogens, and chronic unopposed estrogen exposure raises the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.A: OCPs manage anovulatory bleeding in premenopausal women and would not evaluate for carcinoma.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Postmenopausal bleeding is never reassured away; endometrial pathology must be excluded urgently.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Measuring estradiol delays the tissue diagnosis that postmenopausal bleeding requires.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Deferring imaging for months delays evaluation of a finding that demands urgent workup.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman has had irregular menses for 5 months, followed by hot flashes and vaginal dryness. FSH is elevated on two measurements taken 6 weeks apart, and estradiol is low. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in her evaluation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Annual FSH monitoring without additional testing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Endometrial biopsy of the uterine lining

choices.label: C
choices.text: Karyotype analysis and FMR1 premutation testing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metformin therapy for insulin resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: MRI of the pituitary gland

explanation.summary: Confirmed primary ovarian insufficiency prompts testing for its causes, including karyotype and FMR1 premutation analysis.
explanation.whyCorrect: POI is diagnosed in women under 40 with menstrual irregularity for at least 3 consecutive months and two elevated FSH levels at least 1 month apart, which this patient meets. Once confirmed, testing for causes should include karyotype analysis, FMR1 gene testing for the fragile X premutation, adrenal antibodies, and screening for concurrent autoimmune disorders.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Watchful waiting misses the etiologic workup and delays hormone therapy needed to protect bone and cardiovascular health.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Endometrial biopsy evaluates suspected endometrial pathology from estrogen excess, not estrogen deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metformin treats insulin resistance in PCOS and has no role in primary ovarian insufficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Her elevated FSH localizes the failure to the ovary; a low FSH would instead suggest a central hypothalamic or pituitary cause worth imaging.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is evaluated after a low-impact wrist fracture. He is 203 cm tall, and radiographs show open growth plates and markedly reduced bone density. Serum testosterone and androgen precursors are elevated, estradiol is undetectable, and LH and FSH are elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for his skeletal disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aromatase inhibitor therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Calcium and vitamin D supplementation alone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous estrogen replacement therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gonadotropin therapy with hCG

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone replacement therapy

explanation.summary: In male aromatase deficiency, exogenous estradiol corrects the skeletal abnormalities and closes the epiphyses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elevated testosterone and androgen precursors with undetectable estradiol and elevated gonadotropins confirm aromatase deficiency. This condition demonstrates that estrogens, not androgens alone, are critical for bone health and epiphyseal closure in males, and exogenous estradiol replacement corrects the skeletal abnormalities and closes the epiphyses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An aromatase inhibitor would deepen the estrogen deficiency; these drugs are used to lower estrogen in hyperestrogenic males.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Supplementation does not address the estrogen deficiency driving his unfused epiphyses and osteoporosis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG stimulates endogenous testosterone production for hypogonadal men desiring fertility and does not supply the missing estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.E: His testosterone is already elevated; androgens alone cannot close the epiphyses or restore bone density.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with oligomenorrhea, hirsutism, and acne is counseled that her condition, formerly called polycystic ovary syndrome, is now termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Which of the following is true of how her diagnosis is established?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All three Rotterdam features are now required to be present simultaneously

choices.label: B
choices.text: An elevated DHEA-S level is now required in addition to hyperandrogenism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ovarian cysts must now be documented on two separate ultrasound studies

choices.label: D
choices.text: Polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound is now required in every patient

choices.label: E
choices.text: Two of three Rotterdam features are required after other causes are excluded

explanation.summary: The rename to PMOS reflected the disorder's polyendocrine and metabolic nature but did not alter the diagnostic criteria.
explanation.whyCorrect: PMOS is still diagnosed with the Rotterdam criteria, which require at least two of three features: oligo- or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology on ultrasound, after exclusion of other causes. The name change acknowledged the central role of metabolic dysfunction and removed the misleading implication of cysts, but it explicitly did not change the diagnostic criteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Only two of the three features are needed; requiring all three would exclude many affected patients.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DHEA-S is used to localize androgen excess to an adrenal source, not to make the diagnosis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serial imaging of cysts has never been part of the criteria, and the new name represents ovarian dysfunction without implying cysts.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ovarian morphology is one of three optional features, and the new name was chosen specifically to move away from implying cysts.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman reports five menstrual periods over the past year and facial hirsutism. Free testosterone is elevated, DHEA-S and 17-hydroxyprogesterone are normal, and prolactin and TSH are normal. Transvaginal ultrasound shows normal-appearing ovaries without multiple peripheral follicles. Applying the Rotterdam criteria, which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She cannot be given the PMOS diagnosis because her ovaries appear normal

choices.label: B
choices.text: She does not meet PMOS criteria until a third feature appears

choices.label: C
choices.text: She meets criteria for PMOS on the basis of two features

choices.label: D
choices.text: She should instead be diagnosed with congenital adrenal hyperplasia

choices.label: E
choices.text: She should instead be diagnosed with primary ovarian insufficiency

explanation.summary: Rotterdam requires only two of three features, so normal ovarian morphology does not exclude PMOS.
explanation.whyCorrect: She has oligo-ovulation and biochemical hyperandrogenism, which is two of the three Rotterdam features, and other causes have been excluded by normal 17-OHP, DHEA-S, prolactin, and TSH. Because polycystic ovarian morphology is only one of three features and only two are required, the diagnosis stands despite a normal ultrasound.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ovarian morphology is not mandatory; this is exactly the misconception the rename to PMOS was meant to correct.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Two features already satisfy the criteria; waiting for a third would needlessly delay treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: CAH is screened for with 17-OHP, which is normal here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary ovarian insufficiency causes estrogen-deficiency symptoms with elevated FSH, not hyperandrogenism.

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman with PMOS has had only three or four menstrual periods per year for the past decade. She now reports heavy, prolonged bleeding, and endometrial biopsy shows endometrial hyperplasia. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chronic unopposed estrogen stimulation resulting from anovulation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct stimulation of endometrial growth by excess circulating androgens

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elevated FSH driving proliferation of the endometrial lining

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hyperprolactinemia suppressing the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Profound estrogen deficiency from depletion of ovarian follicles

explanation.summary: Chronic anovulation in PMOS leaves the endometrium under unopposed estrogen, raising hyperplasia and carcinoma risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: Beyond its reproductive consequences, PMOS carries long-term metabolic risks and endometrial hyperplasia from chronic unopposed estrogen exposure. Without ovulation there is no progesterone to oppose estrogen's proliferative effect on the endometrium, so years of anovulatory cycles produce hyperplasia and increase carcinoma risk.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Androgen excess in PMOS produces hirsutism and acne; the endometrial risk comes from unopposed estrogen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FSH is not the driver of endometrial proliferation; estrogen acting without progesterone is.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Hyperprolactinemia causes central hypogonadism with low estrogen, which would not produce hyperplasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen deficiency causes an atrophic, not hyperplastic, endometrium.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman is being evaluated for hirsutism and irregular menses. Which of the following physical findings would be inconsistent with PMOS and should instead prompt evaluation for a virilizing androgen-secreting tumor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Body mass index of 33 kg/m2

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clitoromegaly

choices.label: C
choices.text: Coarse hair on the chin and upper lip

choices.label: D
choices.text: Facial acne

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fewer than nine menses per year

explanation.summary: Clitoromegaly signals virilization and is not a feature of PMOS.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with PMOS commonly have irregular menses, hirsutism, acne, and infertility, and the ovaries may show a string-of-pearls appearance on ultrasound. Unlike patients with virilization, however, they do not have clitoromegaly, so its presence points away from PMOS and toward an androgen-secreting tumor.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Obesity and insulin resistance are typical of the metabolic dysfunction central to PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hirsutism of the chin and upper lip is a classic PMOS finding.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Acne is one of the most common presenting features of PMOS.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Oligomenorrhea reflects the oligo-ovulation that forms one of the Rotterdam features.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old woman with PMOS has taken a combined oral contraceptive for 9 months. Her menses are now regular and her acne has cleared, but coarse terminal hair on her chin and chest continues to require daily removal. Which of the following is the most appropriate addition to her regimen?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anastrozole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Danazol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human chorionic gonadotropin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spironolactone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Transdermal testosterone

explanation.summary: Spironolactone, an androgen receptor blocker, is added for hirsutism that persists on oral contraceptives.
explanation.whyCorrect: In women with PMOS, oral contraceptives are used for hirsutism, acne, and irregular menses, and spironolactone is added for persistent hirsutism because it blocks the androgen receptor. Her menses and acne have responded, so the residual hirsutism is the specific indication for adding an antiandrogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aromatase inhibitors are used to lower estrogen in males with persistent hyperestrogenism, not to treat hirsutism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Danazol is itself a cause of androgen excess in females and would worsen her hirsutism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: hCG stimulates endogenous testosterone production in hypogonadal men desiring fertility.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone is used off-label for hypoactive sexual desire disorder and would aggravate androgen excess.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman has had 5 months of rapidly worsening facial and truncal hair growth, voice deepening, and clitoral enlargement. Total testosterone is markedly elevated, DHEA-S and 17-hydroxyprogesterone are normal, and pelvic ultrasound shows a 4-cm solid right ovarian mass. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Combined oral contraceptive therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metformin for insulin resistance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observation with repeat imaging in 6 months

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spironolactone monotherapy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surgical resection of the ovarian mass

explanation.summary: Androgen-secreting tumors in either sex are treated with surgical resection.
explanation.whyCorrect: Elevated testosterone with a normal DHEA-S localizes the androgen excess to an ovarian source, and rapid virilization with a solid adnexal mass indicates an androgen-secreting ovarian tumor such as a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor. For androgen-secreting tumors in either sex, surgical resection is the treatment of choice.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Oral contraceptives manage the androgen symptoms of PMOS and would leave a tumor in place.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Metformin addresses the insulin resistance of PMOS and has no role against a tumor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Rapid virilization with a solid ovarian mass requires resection rather than surveillance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Blocking the androgen receptor treats hirsutism but does not remove the source of hormone production.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old competitive wrestler admits to injecting anabolic steroids obtained without a prescription to gain muscle mass. Which of the following adverse effects is particularly important to counsel him about because of his age?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Continued long bone growth with unfused epiphyses

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hot flashes and night sweats

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of pubic and axillary hair

choices.label: D
choices.text: Premature cessation of linear growth

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced or absent sense of smell

explanation.summary: In adolescents, anabolic steroids can stop linear growth prematurely.
explanation.whyCorrect: Clinicians should counsel all users of anabolic steroids about adverse effects, and premature growth cessation in adolescents is specifically emphasized as very important to discuss with young users. Other effects he should hear about include mood swings, acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, infertility, cardiac muscle thickening, elevated LDL, and erythrocytosis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Unfused epiphyses with continued growth reflect estrogen deficiency, as in aromatase deficiency, the opposite of this situation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Vasomotor symptoms are the hallmark of estrogen deficiency in women.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of pubic and axillary hair occurs with androgen deficiency in females, not androgen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anosmia is a feature of Kallmann syndrome, unrelated to anabolic steroid use.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man who has used high-dose anabolic steroids for several years is found to have a hematocrit of 58%, an elevated LDL cholesterol, and echocardiographic thickening of the left ventricular wall. Which of the following risks is most directly conferred by his elevated hematocrit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increased risk of bleeding from thrombocytopenia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased risk of hemolytic crisis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased risk of megaloblastic anemia

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased risk of osteoporotic fracture

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased risk of thromboembolism

explanation.summary: Anabolic steroid-induced erythrocytosis increases thromboembolic risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: The cardiovascular adverse effects of anabolic steroids include cardiac muscle thickening, high LDL cholesterol, and erythrocytosis, and the erythrocytosis specifically increases the risk of thromboembolism. His ventricular hypertrophy and dyslipidemia are the other two cardiovascular effects of the same exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Anabolic steroids raise the red cell mass and are not described as causing thrombocytopenia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Hemolysis is not among the described effects; the problem is too many red cells, not their destruction.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Androgens are used medically to stimulate the bone marrow in some anemias, not to cause megaloblastic anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androgen excess does not cause bone loss; osteoporosis accompanies androgen or estrogen deficiency.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man stopped a 4-year course of anabolic steroids 6 weeks ago because he and his wife want to conceive. Semen analysis shows azoospermia, and serum testosterone, LH, and FSH are all low. Which of the following is the most appropriate counseling?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Axis recovery may take months and may require assisted reproduction

choices.label: B
choices.text: His gonadotropins will stay suppressed permanently regardless of treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sperm production should return to normal within about 2 weeks

choices.label: D
choices.text: Spironolactone will speed recovery of his suppressed pituitary output

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone replacement is the fastest way to restore his sperm counts

explanation.summary: After stopping exogenous androgens, HPG axis recovery is slow and assisted reproduction is sometimes needed.
explanation.whyCorrect: In males using exogenous androgens, cessation is the primary intervention, but recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis may take months and sometimes requires assisted reproductive techniques. Six weeks off is far too early to expect restored spermatogenesis given his still-suppressed LH and FSH.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Suppression from exogenous androgens is generally reversible, though slowly.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Two weeks is far shorter than the months the axis typically needs to recover.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Spironolactone is an androgen receptor blocker used for hirsutism and has no role in axis recovery.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone replacement suppresses spermatogenesis and is contraindicated in men desiring fertility.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man treated with chemotherapy for lymphoma 18 months ago reports fatigue and decreased libido. Examination shows small, soft testes. Morning serum testosterone is low on two separate mornings, and LH and FSH are both elevated. Which of the following best classifies his disorder?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Androgen insensitivity syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: Aromatase deficiency

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exogenous androgen use

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hypergonadotropic (primary) hypogonadism

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hypogonadotropic (secondary) hypogonadism

explanation.summary: Low testosterone with elevated gonadotropins indicates primary testicular failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: LH and FSH distinguish primary from secondary hypogonadism: elevated gonadotropins indicate primary testicular failure, while low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins suggest a central cause. Chemotherapy is a listed cause of primary hypogonadism, alongside Klinefelter syndrome, orchitis, testicular torsion, and radiation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Androgen insensitivity shows elevated testosterone with elevated LH.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase deficiency features elevated testosterone with undetectable estradiol and skeletal disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Exogenous androgens raise testosterone while suppressing LH and FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A central cause would produce low or inappropriately normal LH and FSH, not elevated values.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man with a body mass index of 38 kg/m2 who has taken high-dose opioids daily for chronic back pain reports fatigue, low libido, and erectile dysfunction. Morning testosterone is low on two occasions, LH and FSH are low-normal, prolactin is normal, and pituitary MRI is unremarkable. Which of the following best explains his laboratory findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 47,XXY karyotype with seminiferous tubule dysgenesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: An inherited defect in the aromatase enzyme

choices.label: C
choices.text: Functional central suppression of gonadotropin secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Resistance of target tissues to circulating androgens

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testicular failure from acquired primary gonadal injury

explanation.summary: Obesity, opioids, and chronic illness cause secondary hypogonadism by functionally suppressing the HPG axis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Secondary hypogonadism results from hyperprolactinemia, Kallmann syndrome, pituitary tumors, or functional suppression from obesity, opioid use, or chronic illness. His low testosterone with low-normal gonadotropins localizes the problem centrally, and with a normal prolactin and normal pituitary imaging, his opioid use and obesity are the responsible functional suppressors.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Klinefelter syndrome is a primary testicular failure with elevated gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase deficiency presents with skeletal disease, elevated testosterone, and elevated gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Androgen insensitivity is characterized by elevated testosterone with elevated LH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Primary testicular failure produces elevated LH and FSH from loss of negative feedback.

questions.stem: A 42-year-old man has fatigue, decreased libido, and erectile dysfunction. Morning testosterone is low on two occasions with low LH and FSH. Prolactin is normal and pituitary MRI shows no lesion. He also has new-onset diabetes mellitus, arthralgias, bronze skin discoloration, and mildly elevated transaminases. Which of the following studies is most likely to reveal his underlying diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Karyotype analysis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serum DHEA sulfate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Serum hCG and alpha-fetoprotein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serum iron studies

explanation.summary: Iron studies are part of the secondary hypogonadism workup because hemochromatosis can infiltrate the pituitary.
explanation.whyCorrect: In secondary hypogonadism, prolactin, iron studies for hemochromatosis, and pituitary MRI may all be warranted. His diabetes, arthralgias, skin bronzing, and transaminitis together point to iron overload as the systemic cause of his central hypogonadism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Karyotype would identify Klinefelter syndrome, which causes primary hypogonadism with elevated gonadotropins.
whyWrongByChoice.B: 17-OHP screens for congenital adrenal hyperplasia in the workup of androgen excess.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DHEA-S localizes androgen excess to an adrenal source and is not useful in androgen deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.D: hCG and AFP are obtained in men with gynecomastia to exclude a germ cell tumor.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man reports 8 months of fatigue, low mood, and decreased libido. A single nonfasting total testosterone drawn at 4:00 PM is 260 ng/dL. He takes no medications. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Begin intramuscular testosterone replacement therapy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Obtain karyotype analysis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obtain MRI of the pituitary gland

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reassure him that this level is expected for his age

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repeat the testosterone level on a separate morning

explanation.summary: Male hypogonadism requires symptoms plus consistently low morning testosterone on two separate measurements.
explanation.whyCorrect: Diagnosis of male hypogonadism requires both clinical symptoms and consistently low morning serum testosterone levels, typically below 300 ng/dL on two separate measurements. A single afternoon value cannot establish the diagnosis, so the level must be repeated in the morning before therapy or further localization.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Starting replacement before the diagnosis is confirmed commits him to therapy that suppresses spermatogenesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Karyotyping is directed at suspected Klinefelter syndrome once primary testicular failure is documented.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pituitary imaging is reserved for confirmed secondary cases, and gonadotropins have not yet been measured.
whyWrongByChoice.D: His symptoms plus a low value warrant confirmation rather than dismissal as normal aging.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man is evaluated for absent pubertal development due to long-standing androgen deficiency. Compared with a man who develops hypogonadism in his forties, which of the following findings is characteristic of hypogonadism that begins before puberty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased bone mineral density

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased libido

choices.label: C
choices.text: Depressed mood

choices.label: D
choices.text: Eunuchoid body proportions

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced muscle mass

explanation.summary: Prepubertal-onset hypogonadism produces eunuchoid proportions and absent secondary sexual characteristics.
explanation.whyCorrect: When hypogonadism occurs before puberty, it results in delayed or absent pubertal development with small testes, lack of secondary sexual characteristics, and eunuchoid body proportions. Post-pubertal onset instead produces subtler findings that can be mistaken for depression or normal aging.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Decreased bone mineral density is a shared consequence of androgen deficiency regardless of timing.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Decreased libido is a presenting symptom in hypogonadism at any age of onset.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Depressed mood is one of the subtle post-pubertal findings that can be mistaken for depression.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reduced muscle mass occurs in adult-onset hypogonadism as well.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman who has taken a combined oral contraceptive for 2 years reports low libido, fatigue, and a diminished sense of well-being. Menses are regular, estradiol is normal, DHEA-S is normal, total testosterone is low-normal, free testosterone is low, and sex hormone-binding globulin is elevated. Which of the following best explains her low free testosterone?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal insufficiency with loss of adrenal androgen output

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hyperinsulinemia suppressing sex hormone-binding globulin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypopituitarism with loss of gonadotropin secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Loss of ovarian steroid production after follicular depletion

choices.label: E
choices.text: Oral estrogen-induced rise in sex hormone-binding globulin

explanation.summary: Oral contraceptives raise SHBG, which lowers free testosterone and can cause female androgen deficiency.
explanation.whyCorrect: Causes of androgen deficiency in females include bilateral oophorectomy, adrenal insufficiency, hypopituitarism, and use of oral contraceptives, which raise SHBG and thereby reduce free testosterone. Her elevated SHBG with a low free but low-normal total testosterone fits this mechanism exactly, and low libido, fatigue, and reduced well-being are the typical symptoms.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adrenal insufficiency would lower DHEA-S, which is normal here.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Insulin resistance suppresses SHBG and raises free testosterone, the opposite of her pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypopituitarism would also impair estrogen production and disrupt her menstrual cycles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary ovarian insufficiency would cause estrogen deficiency with elevated FSH, but her estradiol and cycles are normal.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old woman who underwent bilateral oophorectomy 6 years ago takes menopausal hormone therapy. Her hot flashes and vaginal dryness have resolved, but she reports persistently absent sexual desire that distresses her and strains her relationship. Which of the following is the most appropriate additional treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increased dose of estradiol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anastrozole, an aromatase inhibitor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Low-dose transdermal testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metformin for insulin resistance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spironolactone at a higher dose

explanation.summary: Low-dose transdermal testosterone is used off-label for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in postmenopausal women.
explanation.whyCorrect: In females, androgen therapy is not FDA-approved but is used off-label for hypoactive sexual desire disorder, particularly in postmenopausal women, using low-dose transdermal testosterone. Recognizing the androgen component of sexual dysfunction matters most in postmenopausal women and those who have undergone oophorectomy, since oophorectomy removes an androgen source as well as an estrogen source.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Her estrogen-dependent symptoms have already resolved, so the residual problem is the androgen component.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Aromatase inhibitors lower estrogen and are used in males with persistent hyperestrogenism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metformin targets insulin resistance in PMOS and has no role in sexual desire disorders.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spironolactone blocks androgen receptors and would worsen androgen deficiency.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman who completed menopause 10 years ago reports breast tenderness and 2 months of vaginal bleeding. Serum estradiol is elevated, and pelvic ultrasound shows a 7-cm solid left adnexal mass with a thickened endometrium. DHEA-S and testosterone are normal. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her estrogen excess?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adrenal adenoma secreting DHEA sulfate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Granulosa cell tumor of the ovary

choices.label: C
choices.text: Impaired hepatic metabolism of estrogens

choices.label: D
choices.text: Peripheral aromatization in adipose tissue

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor of the ovary

explanation.summary: Granulosa cell tumors are estrogen-secreting ovarian neoplasms that cause hyperestrogenism and endometrial stimulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen-secreting ovarian tumors such as granulosa cell tumors are rare but important causes of female estrogen excess, and pelvic ultrasound is used to evaluate for ovarian masses. A solid adnexal mass with elevated estradiol, endometrial thickening, and postmenopausal bleeding fits an estrogen-producing ovarian neoplasm, which is treated by surgical resection.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An adrenal source would raise DHEA-S, which is normal here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Liver disease elevates estrogen by impairing metabolism but would not explain the adnexal mass.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Obesity-related aromatization does not produce a solid ovarian mass.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sertoli-Leydig cell tumors secrete androgens and cause virilization, not estrogen excess.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman has had unpredictable, heavy, prolonged uterine bleeding from chronic anovulatory cycles. Endometrial sampling shows proliferative endometrium without atypia. She had a deep vein thrombosis 2 years ago, so estrogen-containing therapy is not an option. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anastrozole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Combined oral contraceptive pills

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cyclic progestin therapy

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metformin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spironolactone

explanation.summary: Anovulatory hyperestrogenism is managed with progestins to oppose endometrial stimulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: In females, anovulatory hyperestrogenism is managed with progestins, which oppose endometrial stimulation, or with oral contraceptives. Because estrogen excess also increases venous thromboembolic risk and she has already had a deep vein thrombosis, a progestin alone supplies the needed endometrial opposition without adding estrogen.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aromatase inhibitors are used to lower estrogen in males with persistent hyperestrogenism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Combined pills contain estrogen, which is excluded by her thromboembolic history.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metformin targets insulin resistance and does not oppose endometrial stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spironolactone is an antiandrogen used for hirsutism and does not protect the endometrium.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man with a body mass index of 38 kg/m2 is concerned about enlarging breasts. Examination shows bilateral soft, nontender, diffusely fatty enlargement of the chest without any discrete firm tissue beneath the areolae. Serum estradiol, testosterone, LH, and FSH are normal. Which of the following best describes his findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An estrogen-like drug effect at the receptor

choices.label: B
choices.text: An estrogen-secreting Leydig cell tumor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aromatase deficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Glandular gynecomastia from estrogen excess

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pseudogynecomastia

explanation.summary: Fatty chest enlargement without glandular proliferation is pseudogynecomastia, not true gynecomastia.
explanation.whyCorrect: True gynecomastia is benign proliferation of glandular breast tissue and must be distinguished from pseudogynecomastia, which is fatty tissue without glandular proliferation. His soft, diffuse fat without a subareolar glandular disc, together with entirely normal hormone levels, identifies pseudogynecomastia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Drugs such as spironolactone stimulate estrogen receptors and cause true, often painful, glandular enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A Leydig cell tumor would raise estradiol and usually produce true glandular gynecomastia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Aromatase deficiency causes estrogen deficiency with skeletal disease, not breast enlargement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glandular gynecomastia produces firm subareolar tissue and is typically accompanied by hormonal abnormalities.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has bilateral firm subareolar breast tissue, spider angiomata, loss of body hair, and small soft testes. Serum estradiol is elevated. He takes no medications. Which of the following best explains his elevated estradiol?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Absence of aromatase activity in peripheral tissues

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autonomous estradiol secretion by an adrenal adenoma

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen-like stimulation of receptors by a medication

choices.label: D
choices.text: hCG secretion from an occult germ cell tumor

choices.label: E
choices.text: Impaired hepatic metabolism of circulating estrogens

explanation.summary: Liver disease raises estrogen levels by impairing hepatic estrogen metabolism, producing gynecomastia and feminization.
explanation.whyCorrect: Liver cirrhosis is a listed cause of hyperestrogenism in males because impaired hepatic metabolism leaves estrogen levels elevated, which is why liver function tests are part of the evaluation. Prolonged estrogen excess produces feminization with fat redistribution and reduced body hair alongside gynecomastia and testicular suppression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Loss of aromatase activity causes estrogen deficiency with undetectable estradiol, the opposite of his finding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Adrenal pathology is pursued when DHEA-S or cortisol is elevated, which is not indicated here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Drugs such as spironolactone or cimetidine can do this, but he takes no medications, and receptor stimulation would not elevate estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A germ cell tumor is excluded with hCG, AFP, and testicular ultrasound and is not suggested by his cirrhosis and stigmata of liver disease.

questions.stem: A 6-year-old girl is brought in with breast development, pubic hair, and vaginal bleeding. Serum estradiol is markedly elevated. Which of the following consequences of estrogen excess does her presentation represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delayed puberty with eunuchoid proportions

choices.label: B
choices.text: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause

choices.label: C
choices.text: Precocious puberty

choices.label: D
choices.text: Primary ovarian insufficiency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Virilization with clitoromegaly

explanation.summary: Estrogen excess in young females causes precocious puberty.
explanation.whyCorrect: Estrogen excess in young females may cause precocious puberty. In older females the same excess presents with menstrual irregularity, typically heavy or prolonged bleeding from unopposed endometrial stimulation, along with breast tenderness, bloating, and mood changes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Delayed puberty with eunuchoid proportions follows sex hormone deficiency before puberty.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Genitourinary syndrome of menopause reflects estrogen deficiency, with vaginal dryness, dyspareunia, and urinary symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Primary ovarian insufficiency is a state of estrogen deficiency with elevated FSH.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Virilization with clitoromegaly results from androgen, not estrogen, excess.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old elite distance runner with a body mass index of 17 kg/m2 has had no menses for 8 months and now reports hot flashes and vaginal dryness. A pregnancy test is negative and prolactin is normal. Serum estradiol is low and FSH is low. Which of the following best explains her findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autonomous estrogen secretion by an ovarian tumor

choices.label: B
choices.text: Depletion of the ovarian follicular pool

choices.label: C
choices.text: Functional suppression of GnRH secretion

choices.label: D
choices.text: LH-driven ovarian androgen overproduction

choices.label: E
choices.text: Physiologic cessation of ovarian function

explanation.summary: Low estradiol with a low FSH localizes estrogen deficiency to a central hypothalamic or pituitary cause.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypothalamic amenorrhea from excessive exercise, low body weight, or psychological stress causes functional suppression of GnRH and subsequent estrogen deficiency. Diagnostically, a low FSH with low estradiol indicates a central cause, whereas an elevated FSH above roughly 25 to 40 IU/L with low estradiol would instead confirm primary ovarian insufficiency or menopause.

whyWrongByChoice.A: An estrogen-secreting tumor would raise, not lower, her estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Primary ovarian insufficiency would show elevated FSH on two measurements at least 1 month apart.
whyWrongByChoice.D: LH-driven ovarian androgen excess describes PMOS, which presents with hyperandrogenism rather than vasomotor symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Menopause occurs at a mean age of about 51 years and also produces elevated FSH.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman whose last menstrual period was 14 months ago has disruptive hot flashes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, and dyspareunia. Her uterus is intact, and she has no contraindications to hormone therapy. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anastrozole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deferral of hormone therapy for 10 years

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen combined with a progestin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estrogen therapy given alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: Low-dose transdermal testosterone

explanation.summary: Menopausal hormone therapy uses estrogen plus progestin when the uterus is intact, and works best when started early.
explanation.whyCorrect: Menopausal hormone therapy with estrogen, combined with a progestin in women with an intact uterus, effectively treats vasomotor symptoms and prevents bone loss. The progestin opposes endometrial stimulation, since chronic unopposed estrogen raises the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma, and therapy is most beneficial when initiated within 10 years of menopause onset.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aromatase inhibitors lower estrogen and would worsen every one of her symptoms.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Delaying forfeits the window in which therapy is most beneficial, within 10 years of menopause onset.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Unopposed estrogen in a woman with a uterus exposes the endometrium to hyperplasia and carcinoma risk.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Testosterone is used off-label for hypoactive sexual desire disorder, not for vasomotor symptoms.

questions.stem: A 46-year-old man with painful bilateral glandular gynecomastia has lost 40 pounds and stopped cimetidine over the past year. Testicular ultrasound, hCG, AFP, and liver function tests are all normal, but serum estradiol remains elevated and the breast tissue is unchanged and still tender. Which of the following is the most appropriate next treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anastrozole

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cyclic progestin therapy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Intramuscular testosterone

choices.label: D
choices.text: Metformin

choices.label: E
choices.text: Spironolactone

explanation.summary: Aromatase inhibitors lower estrogen in males with hyperestrogenism that persists after the root cause is addressed.
explanation.whyCorrect: In males, treatment first targets the root cause with weight loss for obesity-related aromatization, discontinuation of offending medications, or tumor resection. When hyperestrogenism persists despite these measures, aromatase inhibitors such as anastrozole can reduce estrogen levels, and his tumor and hepatic workups are already negative.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Progestins are used to oppose endometrial stimulation in anovulatory women.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Exogenous androgen provides more substrate for aromatization and suppresses the HPG axis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Metformin treats insulin resistance in PMOS and does not lower estradiol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Spironolactone stimulates estrogen receptors and is itself a cause of gynecomastia in men.
